title: When a restart is needed
text: When a restart is needed A superclass change needs a restart. On a stock JVM, arbitrary reflection cannot discover members added after startup. Changing a method body preserves existing object fields. A Spring bean refresh can recreate the bean and reset its mutable state. Understand state during a reload How it works / Tested with The agent watches compiled output and applies supported bytecode changes. Framework integrations then refresh supported beans, mappings and metadata. Docs for 1.7.0. Each result has its own runtime and framework scope. Read the recorded versions and test coverage . Read the architecture

title: Your first reload
text: Before you start Use a development application on Java 17 or later. Choose a matching agent and integration version available in your release channel. Use one attachment route per JVM. Installing the plugin alone does not attach to an application that is already running. Check your runtime and artifact requirements Choose how you start the application IntelliJ IntelliJ + SAP Gradle Maven Java agent IntelliJ: use an IDE-managed Java run Install Reclazz in Settings → Plugins → Marketplace , or install the release ZIP from disk. Compile with the build that writes the watched module outputs. Open the Reclazz tool window. Call the same endpoint or method again without restarting. For delegated Gradle or Maven runs, use the corresponding tab. Other plugin installation routes Read optional command-line plugin installation . Still enable the plugin for your project afterward. title: If the result did not change
text: If the result did not change Start with the watched output and diagnostic checks . A connected agent or successful compile is not enough. How it works / Tested with Docs for 1.7.0. Java 17+ is a target; runtime coverage is specific to each version and environment. The 30-second delay applies to startup attachment. Dynamic attachment begins watching immediately. Use the complete verification recipe when you need class/hash receipts as well as application behavior.

title: Edit an existing method body
text: Method-body edits reload when compiled into a watched output. Existing object fields stay in place on the JVM-only path. A separate framework refresh can recreate beans. Compile the edit, repeat the original operation and check the changed result in the same JVM.

title: Add or remove a method
text: Added or removed methods work through hot-compiled callers on a stock JDK. They are not native members of the original Class. A caller using a removed method gets NoSuchMethodError, or the inherited implementation for a removed override, as after restart. Compile affected watched callers. Use a supported framework adapter when the operation needs reflection.

title: Add an instance field
text: Stock mode stores added fields separately. Isolated initializers run on first read for existing objects; constructor-dependent or entangled initializers retain type defaults with a reason. Read the initializer diagnostic and verify an existing object.

title: Read/write an added field from another class
text: Both owner and caller must be watched/reloaded in the measured direct-access shape. Field-type changes and every inherited/loader variant are not certified. Compile both sides and check the shared value on an existing object.

title: Add a static field with an initializer
text: Compile-time constants and separable initializers, including bounded forward conditionals/switches, are supported. Other static blocks and current added-field values are preserved. Check the new value and any extraction refusal reason.

title: Change an already initialized static field initializer
text: resetStatics=true at startup; an existing prepared physical field with a changed isolated pure initializer. Frozen first-load definalization is reflection-visible. Added fields keep execute-once behavior. Check the reset/refusal diagnostic; restart for captured aliases, constants, missing preparation or refused expressions.

title: Change an inlined compile-time constant
text: Callers can retain their old literal until recompiled. AutoCompile can rebuild detected watched sources; unwatched consumers remain outside that repair. Recompile affected callers or use supported AutoCompile.

title: Append an enum constant / remove its final constant
text: Documented on JDK 17–25 with ordinal-preserving edits. Existing application arrays sized from the old enum length do not grow. Check enum consumers and any fixed-size application arrays.

title: Insert/reorder enum values or remove a non-tail value
text: The edit renumbers ordinals; Reclazz refuses it. Restart alone does not migrate persisted ordinal data. Review persisted ordinals and restart for the type change.

title: Add or remove an implemented interface
text: Requires a compatible enhanced-redefinition JVM such as JBR/DCEVM. Stock JVMs refuse the type change. Use a supported enhanced runtime or restart.

title: Change a superclass
text: The loaded superclass stays unchanged. Eligible bodies may apply; dependent methods stay pinned and unsafe signatures/constructors can refuse the whole save. Read partial/refused reporting and restart for the hierarchy.

title: Discover added members through arbitrary reflection
text: On stock JVMs the original Class lacks companion members. Explicit framework adapters have separate scope; arbitrary reflective consumers do not. Restart, or use a compatible enhanced JVM/explicitly supported adapter.

title: Assume every Java 17+ vendor/version is certified
text: Java 17+ is the target, not certification of every runtime. The main portable records cover stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64. Validate your exact runtime and edit shape.

title: Refresh an affected singleton bean
text: Supported singleton paths recreate the affected bean and repair supported references. Mutable state can reset. Arbitrary external holders are not repaired. Check lifecycle effects and the result served through an existing application reference.

title: Add a new component class
text: New direct or composed component classes use native naming and registration-time conditions. Singleton, prototype and lazy creation are supported. Full startup scanning is not repeated. Compile the new class and check its registration and condition result.

title: Add a component with a web/custom scope or scoped proxy
text: The new-component path refuses these scope shapes. Normal singleton/prototype support does not imply custom scope enrollment. Restart under the application’s normal configuration.

title: Reevaluate every filtered component after a profile/property edit
text: New-component conditions are evaluated at registration. General rediscovery after a profile/property edit and replay of startup imports or auto-configuration are outside this path. Restart for changed startup topology, or validate the narrower path you use.

title: Add an @Bean factory method
text: Supported lite, full and static configuration paths can register added factory methods. Arguments, aliases, selection and direct conditions have a defined allowlist. Existing names, custom scopes and unknown composed conditions remain restricted. Check the factory allowlist, then verify product identity and lifecycle.

title: Change existing injection or lifecycle metadata
text: Spring metadata caches are refreshed on supported bean paths. Recreation has state and reference limits; it is not an arbitrary graph rewrite. Check the recreated bean’s injection and lifecycle behavior.

title: Add @PostConstruct / @PreDestroy methods
text: Supported plain singletons use the javax Spring 5 / Jakarta Spring 6 lanes. Each instance keeps its added destroy callback through later edits/removal. Verify creation/injection/destruction for the affected instance.

title: Add @Transactional or cache-advised service methods
text: Supported public singleton operations use native interceptors; bounded composed metadata is supported. Compile the caller and respect the proxy/advice allowlist. Verify commit/rollback or cache behavior, not only the method result.

title: Add pre/post authorization to a new service operation
text: Named classic/modern Spring Security graphs support direct and bounded composed policies. Unknown security infrastructure/advice shapes are refused. Check both allowed and denied calls with the installed security graph.

title: Edit an @Aspect pointcut
text: Updates supported existing mutable singleton JDK/CGLIB proxy chains. Previously unproxied targets and unsupported proxy shapes are outside this path. Check an already-injected reference and inspect unsupported targets.

title: Add/edit/remove @Scheduled methods
text: Direct no-argument void callbacks on supported singletons, with documented proxy/transaction/cache/async combinations. Removal cancels the registration. Check one current schedule and retirement of its predecessor.

title: Add/edit/remove @EventListener methods
text: Direct callbacks with one reference event input and void/single-event return on supported singletons. Filtering/order/conditions and advice have bounded scope. Publish a test event; check current delivery and no stale registration.

title: Add @TransactionalEventListener methods
text: Direct void methods on supported unproxied singletons; Spring handles phase/fallback/conditions/order. Reload retires queued callbacks from the old added registration. Check the intended transaction phase and a later edit/removal.

title: Add @Async service methods
text: Direct public methods support void, Future and CompletableFuture with native executor/error handling and supported transaction/cache advice. Check execution, returned completion and exception handling.

title: Reload a helper captured by a constructor-injected leaf
text: Exact supported factories, plain two-node shapes and one measured direct-child context form. Aliases, broader graphs, proxies/factory products and lifecycle-owned shapes are excluded. Read the ownership contract and verify the retained caller’s value.

title: Add/change a controller endpoint
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Supported mapping rescans discover changed endpoints, including added methods on a stock JVM. Receiver, metadata and classloader restrictions still apply. Compile the controller and send a request to the intended route.

title: Add @ExceptionHandler methods
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Plain controllers/advice and standard resolver on Framework 5.3.39/6.1.14; bounded synchronous metadata. Proxy/inheritance/generic/composed/custom resolver shapes are excluded. Check status/body and handler precedence; fix ambiguous mappings.

title: Add @InitBinder / @ModelAttribute methods
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Supported plain controller/advice adapters preserve named binding, model rules and native advice order/selectors. Read the exact callback allowlist. Check a real binding/model request through the current controller.

title: Add Jackson getters, setters or DTO fields
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Supported Spring-managed mapper adapter; mutable DTOs and saved annotations. Final added fields are not writable; creator/record/builder additions are excluded. Check JSON input and output against the installed Jackson version.

title: Assume every serializer discovers companion members
text: The explicit Jackson adapter does not establish support for arbitrary Gson/custom mappers or record creators. On stock JVMs, original-class reflection remains limited. Validate the serializer or restart when native reflective visibility is required.

title: Change validation constraints on an existing field
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Supported Hibernate Validator metadata caches are cleared in both javax/Jakarta factory discovery paths. Do not infer arbitrary validator/provider compatibility. Submit both invalid and valid input; inspect the native validation result.

title: Edit an existing Spring Security HTTP rule
section: Web & JSON · Reloads, with a condition
text: Supported SecurityFilterChain beans rebuild into the live FilterChainProxy. Inline ignoring chains remain; a failed rebuild can keep the previous rules serving. Verify allowed and denied requests; inspect whether the new rules became live.

title: Add/edit/remove a Kafka listener
text: Plain singleton, direct callback, explicit literal ID, documented topic/group/options and standard record-mode factory. Native consumers retire before replacement. Verify message delivery, new route and old-consumer retirement.

title: Add/edit/remove a JMS listener
text: Plain singleton with standard processor/registry/default container factory. Literal or placeholder destinations/selectors; bounded result and callback shapes. Verify delivery/selector behavior and complete consumer destruction.

title: Add synchronous JMS replies
text: Documented return types and direct @SendTo. JMSReplyTo takes priority; null sends nothing. No arbitrary DTO/Future/reactive return claim. Check conversion, correlation and destination on a test request.

title: Add/edit/remove a Rabbit listener
text: Plain receiver, standard simple container, AUTO acknowledgment/default executor and bounded queue/options. Startup worker hook must track complete retirement. Wait for worker retirement and verify real message delivery.

title: Change a Kafka/Rabbit expression-driven route
text: Documented native SpEL values are reevaluated when the listener is saved. Evaluation occurs after old consumers retire and can fail without restoring them. Save the listener again and check the exact route/group.

title: Reroute consumers by changing only a routing property/bean
text: The documented added Kafka/Rabbit expression path does not automatically reroute on a property/bean-only edit; a listener re-save is the supported live action. Re-save/compile the listener, or restart for native startup resolution.

title: Recreate JMS/Kafka consumers after a helper/property save
text: Separately measured narrow root-context leaf-owner transactions; exact factories, constructor and callback shapes. Not arbitrary consumer graphs. Use the constructor ownership guide and check current-value delivery.

title: Recreate Rabbit consumers through property/dependency cascades
text: Measured on Framework 5.3.39/AMQP 2.4.17 and Framework 6.1.14/AMQP 3.1.7, stock JDK 17/21 on macOS arm64: one root context, plain local helper/leaf owner, one void literal-ID callback, native simple containers, AUTO acknowledgment and nontransacted channels. Verify current helper/owner values and complete worker retirement; unsupported ownership, stop timeout or partial reconstruction requires restart.

title: Reload one bean mixing Kafka/JMS/Rabbit consumers
text: Unsupported mixed ownership is refused before owned consumers retire. Single-broker coordination is not a combined broker transaction. Separate the ownership shape or restart.

title: Assume XA, hosted clusters, rebalances or exactly-once reload
text: Local broker observations do not certify hosted clusters, failure modes, transactional topology, rebalances or exactly-once reload. Rabbit reply/async and broader custom-container paths remain separate gaps. Validate your broker, lifecycle and delivery policy with targeted acceptance.

title: Edit recognized Boot properties
text: Recognized Boot properties are checked for binding, conversion and validation before live mutation. Invalid or uncheckable input stays pending. Setter or recreation failure can partially apply. Fix rejected input and save again. Inspect the actual runtime values, including after a partial failure.

title: Edit nested YAML values or indexed lists
text: Already-loaded local Boot resources with stable source/document ownership. Current native lane is Boot 2.7.18 / SnakeYAML 1.30, not all Boot versions. Edit the actual runtime file and inspect source precedence.

title: Delete a key or a recognized Boot file
text: Removal reveals lower-priority values/defaults in the supported source path. Mutable property identities are preserved; read-only/write-only removal shapes are uncheckable. Verify resulting defaults and supported consumer rebinding.

title: Change active documents, imports, profiles or config locations
text: Stable source positions/document activation are prerequisites. Startup config topology is not rebuilt by a value save. Restart with the new startup configuration.

title: Change direct or computed @Value inputs
text: Direct and supported computed values can update through their field, constructor or factory path. Each consumer has its own checks and recreation rules. Unsupported expression operations hold the candidate. Check the expression and consumer shape before retrying.

title: Edit a property on a loaded ordinary XML bean
text: Resolved local file/context ownership plus supported value shape. Setter errors can preserve metadata but still have application side effects. Inspect the property result and independent-bean diagnostics.

title: Edit existing XML constructor/factory/lifecycle metadata
text: Bounded ordinary singleton recreation, stable concrete type/ownership and supported direct holders. Native observer: Spring 5.3.39 / JDK 21. Check creation/destruction, repaired references and any restore failure.

title: Change XML scope, parent, aliases or creation policy
text: Existing metadata changes such as depends-on/primary/autowire/effective lazy flag are guarded. Supported property edits do not rebuild startup policy. Follow the bean-specific restart diagnostic.

title: Save unchanged unsupported XML definitions
text: A proven unchanged standard definition stays quiet, including known abstract/prototype shapes. Unknown/custom metadata retains conservative diagnostics. Expect no reconstruction; real unsupported edits still require restart.

title: Edit newly imported, remote or packaged XML
text: Captured-local discovery does not cover remote/JAR resources, pre-hook loads or a general import-topology rebuild. Edit the actually owned local resource or restart.

title: Edit recognized physical message bundles
text: Named native Spring message-source/cache lanes; arbitrary custom basenames and automatic source-to-output copying are not established. Edit the runtime file and check a warmed formatted lookup.

title: Edit recognized file templates
text: Named FreeMarker/Thymeleaf file-resolver lanes. Malformed saves can produce render errors; last-valid retention is not promised. Render the current output; fix malformed input and retry.

title: Edit resources inside packaged JAR/WAR files
text: Physical-file observers do not establish packaged-resource replacement or arbitrary view-resolver integration. Use unpacked recognized runtime resources or restart/redeploy.

title: Change a supported logging level/configuration
text: Supported logging.level keys or logback/log4j2 config refresh. Removing a level without a fallback can still need reset/restart. Verify the target logger; keep SAP property pairs separate.

title: Expect arbitrary files to trigger a reload
text: Reclazz recognizes specific suffixes and owned resources. It takes no reload action for an unknown kind. Your framework may independently serve that file. Check the resource classifier and your application’s resource pipeline.

title: Add a mapped field to an existing entity
text: Requires enhanced visibility plus supported jpaRefresh=true/DDL-enabled mapping path; stock companion fields are not native ORM members. Prepare schema/mapping prerequisites or restart.

title: Add a new JPA entity with a prepared schema
text: jpaRefresh=true, explicit Hibernate validate, one unit and standard provider/factory in the recorded graph. No automatic migration or update-mode switch. Prepare table/columns, compile and verify native mapping installation.

title: Retry a new-entity mapping after a schema failure
text: Failed candidate leaves the previous factory open before install. Identical bytes are ignored; changing pending mapping declarations is refused. Fix schema, then compile a body-only edit to the same pending entity.

title: Keep old persistence contexts/transactions through a rebuild
text: A successful persistence-unit swap retires the old native factory. Holding active old contexts across it is unsupported. Finish database work first; restart/recover unsupported retained contexts.

title: Edit supported Spring Data query methods
text: Warm singleton Repository products and bounded direct holder repair. Scalar H2 native-query evidence does not cover new interface methods/all query shapes. Check the query result and the retained managed consumer.

title: Invalidate caches dependent on changed helper code
text: Observed synchronous Spring cache dependencies in stock companion mode; region-level conservative eviction. Async/unwatched/pre-attach work is not complete. Exercise the cache first, reload and check next-call freshness.

title: Rebuild a custom cache owner after helper changes
text: refreshOwnersOnHelper opt-in for supported singleton owners. Non-singletons, FactoryBeans and event-listener owners are declined. Name the eligible owner and check lifecycle/state reset.

title: Save *-items.xml / *-beans.xml
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Platform generation and builds can reload the generated classes. Persistence, type-system updates and native reflection are separate requirements. Check generated bytecode. Apply the platform schema update when required.

title: Create columns through Update Running System
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Manual HAC action is separate from reload. autoUpdateRunningSystem=true is a distinct off-by-default dev-only DDL opt-in. Choose the schema action explicitly and verify the type/persistence result.

title: Apply changed SAP configuration keys
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Changed keys reach the native Config path and acknowledge independently when successful. A startup-only consumer still needs a restart. Check each key’s runtime consumer and pending status.

title: Edit type/enum localization or Backoffice labels
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Recognized physical locale/label files refresh the platform caches they serve. Broader tenant/cluster acceptance is not implied. Check a new lookup or reopen the affected Backoffice view.

title: Import a changed ImpEx file automatically
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: autoImpex=true opt-in writes live development data. REMOVE/macro-expanded REMOVE is refused unless separately permitted; no rollback. Use disposable data; inspect import results and guard diagnostics.

title: Refresh supported interceptor mappings
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Mappings and native registry identities survive interceptor bean refresh. Watched XML additions and setter-defined interceptor ref/typeCode edits reconcile each owner’s context and ModelService registries. Mapping definitions requiring recreation, and unsupported removal, need a restart. Check the registry result and a relevant live model operation.

title: Edit OCC field sets, mappings or supported directives
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Dedicated field-set/request-mapping/populator/list-merge paths have individual ownership and registration limits. Not arbitrary platform topology reload. Read the matching path and verify the actual OCC response.

title: Add an extension to the platform
text: The extension list is established at startup. Generated-bytecode reload does not enroll a new extension. Build the platform and restart.

title: Edit *-backoffice-config.xml
text: Runs the native F4 cockpit-config reset in the owning tenant/session, rebuilding persisted configuration from module sources. This also resets configuration changed in the UI; widgets are not reset. Disable with backofficeConfigReset=false. Open a new view; disabled or failed resets report WARN instead of success.

title: Add a Backoffice @SocketEvent action
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Requires an agent-prepared class; standard modules follow the backoffice-module admission conditions. Generic reflection lets newly composed default MVC components bind public non-static handlers with at most one parameter. One-parameter native detached dispatch measured on JDK17/21; local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified a new view binding, retained open-view binding, body edit and removal without stale dispatch. Open components retain bindings. Compose a new view. Invalid native signatures keep PENDING; static reload is unverified and keeps PENDING. Removed added methods stop stale dispatch.

title: Reload a Java Backoffice module
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: Explicit backoffice-module=true metadata, selected extension and exact WidgetClassLoader; one owning backoffice/classes file with identical initial bytes. Source compilation and IDE output saves are tested with a synthetic opaque loader; preparation and added-method reload measured with both native SDK loaders. Start with the agent before the class loads. Rebuild stale output/JAR bytes and restart if initial admission fails. Duplicate definitions remain unprepared; reload targets only the prepared owner. Local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified startup preparation and source-to-widget handler add/edit/removal; broader widget routing remains unverified.

title: Edit an observed process XML or add a new process XML/resource bean
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: With the SAP automation module, a new name can be published into a warm standard native cache only from an exact resource singleton added by a watched, observed Spring source. Both save orders are supported. Unproven siblings, duplicate/existing names, dynamic definitions and replaced owners are refused. Each proven native owner is evaluated in its own tenant/session scope; failures and proof retirement stay local to that owner. Cold caches retain native lazy loading. Proven later edits preserve historical versions; deletion requires restart. Verify a newly started process. Already started processes keep their version within this JVM; no migration, replay, cache-eviction retention or cluster propagation.

title: Add a new dependency JAR to the JVM classpath
text: The running JVM startup classpath is not replaced by watching class outputs. Restart with the updated launch classpath.

title: Refresh stored documents after an indexing provider/resolver reload
section: SAP Commerce · Reloads, with a condition
text: autoSolrReindex=true, SAP module, exact provider metadata, stock local standalone provider/strategy, explicit stored PKs and 10,000-document limit. Property providers use partial updates; type resolvers use whole-document UPDATE. Normal native listeners and operation bookkeeping still run. Verify the stored search field separately from the class reload receipt. Unknown targets, missing cores, remote/cluster mode and incomplete reads are refused.

title: Avoid a supported request crossing a method-body reload
text: reloadBoundary=request at startup, supported native MVC hook/lifetimes. Drain deadline defers; it is not batch/schema/background atomicity. Check the measured servlet graph and queued-work diagnostics.

title: Apply class output from a failed/paused build
text: Build admission holds output until a successful captured batch; SCAN alone cannot release the hold. Manual pause is an independent switch. Complete the build, release the correct hold and verify completion.

title: What reloads

Broader tenant/cluster acceptance is not implied. Next: Check a new lookup or reopen the affected Backoffice view. REMOVE/macro-expanded REMOVE is refused unless separately permitted; no rollback. Next: Use disposable data; inspect import results and guard diagnostics. Refresh supported interceptor mappings Reloads, with a condition Mappings and native registry identities survive interceptor bean refresh. Watched XML additions and setter-defined interceptor ref/typeCode edits reconcile each owner’s context and ModelService registries. Mapping definitions requiring recreation, and unsupported removal, need a restart. Next: Check the registry result and a relevant live model operation. Edit OCC field sets, mappings or supported directives Reloads, with a condition Dedicated field-set/request-mapping/populator/list-merge paths have individual ownership and registration limits. Not arbitrary platform topology reload. Next: Read the matching path and verify the actual OCC response. Edit *-backoffice-config.xml Reloads Runs the native F4 cockpit-config reset in the owning tenant/session, rebuilding persisted configuration from module sources. This also resets configuration changed in the UI; widgets are not reset. Disable with backofficeConfigReset=false. Next: Open a new view; disabled or failed resets report WARN instead of success. Add a Backoffice @SocketEvent action Reloads, with a condition Requires an agent-prepared class; standard modules follow the backoffice-module admission conditions. Generic reflection lets newly composed default MVC components bind public non-static handlers with at most one parameter. One-parameter native detached dispatch measured on JDK17/21; local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified a new view binding, retained open-view binding, body edit and removal without stale dispatch. Open components retain bindings. Next: Compose a new view. Invalid native signatures keep PENDING; static reload is unverified and keeps PENDING. Removed added methods stop stale dispatch. Reload a Java Backoffice module Reloads, with a condition Explicit backoffice-module=true metadata, selected extension and exact WidgetClassLoader; one owning backoffice/classes file with identical initial bytes. Source compilation and IDE output saves are tested with a synthetic opaque loader; preparation and added-method reload measured with both native SDK loaders. Next: Start with the agent before the class loads. Rebuild stale output/JAR bytes and restart if initial admission fails. Duplicate definitions remain unprepared; reload targets only the prepared owner. Local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified startup preparation and source-to-widget handler add/edit/removal; broader widget routing remains unverified. Edit an observed process XML or add a new process XML/resource bean Reloads, with a condition With the SAP automation module, a new name can be published into a warm standard native cache only from an exact resource singleton added by a watched, observed Spring source. Both save orders are supported. Unproven siblings, duplicate/existing names, dynamic definitions and replaced owners are refused. Each proven native owner is evaluated in its own tenant/session scope; failures and proof retirement stay local to that owner. Cold caches retain native lazy loading. Proven later edits preserve historical versions; deletion requires restart. Next: Verify a newly started process. Already started processes keep their version within this JVM; no migration, replay, cache-eviction retention or cluster propagation. Refresh stored documents after an indexing provider/resolver reload Reloads, with a condition autoSolrReindex=true, SAP module, exact provider metadata, stock local standalone provider/strategy, explicit stored PKs and 10,000-document limit. Property providers use partial updates; type resolvers use whole-document UPDATE. Normal native listeners and operation bookkeeping still run. Next: Verify the stored search field separately from the class reload receipt. Unknown targets, missing cores, remote/cluster mode and incomplete reads are refused. Add an extension to the platform Needs a restart The extension list is established at startup. Generated-bytecode reload does not enroll a new extension. Next: Build the platform and restart.

title: Messaging: verify delivery after the save
text: Messaging: verify delivery after the save Keep a known listener ID and a test message. After compiling, verify the new route, current handler result and retirement of the old consumer. Your changes and their conditions Your change Result Before you try it Add/edit/remove a Kafka listener Reloads, with a condition Plain singleton, direct callback, explicit literal ID, documented topic/group/options and standard record-mode factory. Native consumers retire before replacement. Next: Verify message delivery, new route and old-consumer retirement. Add/edit/remove a JMS listener Reloads, with a condition Plain singleton with standard processor/registry/default container factory. Literal or placeholder destinations/selectors; bounded result and callback shapes. Next: Verify delivery/selector behavior and complete consumer destruction. Add synchronous JMS replies Reloads, with a condition Documented return types and direct @SendTo. JMSReplyTo takes priority; null sends nothing. No arbitrary DTO/Future/reactive return claim. Next: Check conversion, correlation and destination on a test request. Add/edit/remove a Rabbit listener Reloads, with a condition Plain receiver, standard simple container, AUTO acknowledgment/default executor and bounded queue/options. Startup worker hook must track complete retirement. Next: Wait for worker retirement and verify real message delivery. Change a Kafka/Rabbit expression-driven route Reloads, with a condition Documented native SpEL values are reevaluated when the listener is saved. Evaluation occurs after old consumers retire and can fail without restoring them. Next: Save the listener again and check the exact route/group. Reroute consumers by changing only a routing property/bean Reloads, with a condition The documented added Kafka/Rabbit expression path does not automatically reroute on a property/bean-only edit; a listener re-save is the supported live action. Next: Re-save/compile the listener, or restart for native startup resolution. Recreate JMS/Kafka consumers after a helper/property save Reloads, with a condition Separately measured narrow root-context leaf-owner transactions; exact factories, constructor and callback shapes. Not arbitrary consumer graphs. Next: Use the constructor ownership guide and check current-value delivery. Recreate Rabbit consumers through property/dependency cascades Reloads, with a condition Measured on Framework 5.3.39/AMQP 2.4.17 and Framework 6.1.14/AMQP 3.1.7, stock JDK 17/21 on macOS arm64: one root context, plain local helper/leaf owner, one void literal-ID callback, native simple containers, AUTO acknowledgment and nontransacted channels. Next: Verify current helper/owner values and complete worker retirement; unsupported ownership, stop timeout or partial reconstruction requires restart. Reload one bean mixing Kafka/JMS/Rabbit consumers Needs a restart Unsupported mixed ownership is refused before owned consumers retire. Single-broker coordination is not a combined broker transaction. Next: Separate the ownership shape or restart. Assume XA, hosted clusters, rebalances or exactly-once reload Not verified yet Local broker observations do not certify hosted clusters, failure modes, transactional topology, rebalances or exactly-once reload. Rabbit reply/async and broader custom-container paths remain separate gaps. Next: Validate your broker, lifecycle and delivery policy with targeted acceptance. Reevaluate every filtered component after a profile/property edit Not verified yet New-component conditions are evaluated at registration. General rediscovery after a profile/property edit and replay of startup imports or auto-configuration are outside this path. Next: Restart for changed startup topology, or validate the narrower path you use. Assume every serializer discovers companion members Not verified yet The explicit Jackson adapter does not establish support for arbitrary Gson/custom mappers or record creators. On stock JVMs, original-class reflection remains limited. Next: Validate the serializer or restart when native reflective visibility is required.

Other static blocks and current added-field values are preserved. Next: Check the new value and any extraction refusal reason. Change an already initialized static field initializer Reloads, with a condition resetStatics=true at startup; an existing prepared physical field with a changed isolated pure initializer. Frozen first-load definalization is reflection-visible. Added fields keep execute-once behavior. Next: Check the reset/refusal diagnostic; restart for captured aliases, constants, missing preparation or refused expressions. Change an inlined compile-time constant Reloads, with a condition Callers can retain their old literal until recompiled. AutoCompile can rebuild detected watched sources; unwatched consumers remain outside that repair. Next: Recompile affected callers or use supported AutoCompile. Append an enum constant / remove its final constant Reloads, with a condition Documented on JDK 17–25 with ordinal-preserving edits. Existing application arrays sized from the old enum length do not grow. Next: Check enum consumers and any fixed-size application arrays. Insert/reorder enum values or remove a non-tail value Needs a restart The edit renumbers ordinals; Reclazz refuses it. Restart alone does not migrate persisted ordinal data. Next: Review persisted ordinals and restart for the type change. Add or remove an implemented interface Reloads, with a condition Requires a compatible enhanced-redefinition JVM such as JBR/DCEVM. Stock JVMs refuse the type change. Next: Use a supported enhanced runtime or restart. Change a superclass Needs a restart The loaded superclass stays unchanged. Eligible bodies may apply; dependent methods stay pinned and unsafe signatures/constructors can refuse the whole save. Next: Read partial/refused reporting and restart for the hierarchy. Discover added members through arbitrary reflection Needs a restart On stock JVMs the original Class lacks companion members. Explicit framework adapters have separate scope; arbitrary reflective consumers do not. Next: Restart, or use a compatible enhanced JVM/explicitly supported adapter. Assume every Java 17+ vendor/version is certified Not verified yet Java 17+ is the target, not certification of every runtime. The main portable records cover stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64. Next: Validate your exact runtime and edit shape.

title: Restart needed when
text: Restart needed when Superclass changes, ordinal-changing enum edits and unsupported reflective access have explicit restart results above.

title: Terms you may see
text: Terms you may see Stock JDK A standard JVM without enhanced class redefinition. Companion A hidden helper class used for added members on a stock JVM. It does not add native members to the original Class. JetBrains Runtime (JBR) A runtime with an enhanced redefinition path when supported and enabled. Check your runtime before using its flags. title: When a change doesn’t reload
text: Nothing happened after an edit Open Reclazz and check that it is connected to the application you are testing. Open Settings → Tools → Reclazz and check that the plugin was enabled before the IDE-managed launch. External servers need their own attachment route. Compile with the build that writes the watched class output. For Gradle Boot use ./gradlew classes ; for Maven use mvn compile ; for SAP use your platform ant build . Wait for startup watching: the default delay is 30 seconds. Dynamic attach does not have that wait. In the editor, choose Tools → Why Didn't My Class Reload? . It reports the class outcome and byte source. The protocol equivalent is DIAGNOSE <class> . Check the full first-reload sequence The log says reloaded, but behavior is old Repeat the same application request in the same JVM. A class event alone does not prove the served result. Use Why Didn't My Class Reload? to check the class and output path, then inspect the framework effects in the Reload Log. Check the condition for your edit . A recreated Spring bean may reset state; arbitrary external references may still hold an old object. State and reference limits Reclazz says a restart is needed Choose Tools

title: Reclazz says a restart is needed
text: Reclazz says a restart is needed Choose Tools → What Still Needs a Restart? . The protocol equivalent is PENDING . Read the reason for the affected change. Restart when the required hierarchy, reflection or framework step cannot be applied. For a bad method implementation, restore the old source and compile again. Source reversal does not undo destroyed resources or schema changes. Recovery and diagnostics reference

title: A SAP model field is missing at runtime
text: A SAP model field is missing at runtime Check the generated class output after the platform build. Saving items.xml is not the same as installing a database column. Check the type-system/schema update and native reflective visibility separately. Follow the persistence guide for the mapping path, and use the required platform update or restart. Generated classes and schema conditions

title: The IDE is not connected
text: The IDE is not connected Check Settings → Tools → Reclazz → Enable Reclazz . Start the application through the route you configured. For a SAP server already running without an agent, use Tools → Attach Reclazz to Running Server . The IDE and server must use the same OS user, with the attach module available. Use Tools → How Is Reclazz Doing? after connecting to inspect watched work and failures. The protocol equivalent is HEALTH . Dynamic attach requirements How it works / Tested with Docs for 1.7.0. Diagnostic commands require matching agent/client builds. Names such as VERIFY and PENDING are protocol commands, not bare shell commands. For exact class-byte acceptance, follow the baseline, DOCTOR and VERIFY recipe , then confirm application behavior in the same JVM. Command syntax and fields . Find the local socket .

title: An edit is waiting for a request or build
text: An edit is waiting for a request or build Your changes and their conditions Your change Result Before you try it Avoid a supported request crossing a method-body reload Reloads, with a condition reloadBoundary=request at startup, supported native MVC hook/lifetimes. Drain deadline defers; it is not batch/schema/background atomicity. Next: Check the measured servlet graph and queued-work diagnostics. Apply class output from a failed/paused build Reloads, with a condition Build admission holds output until a successful captured batch; SCAN alone cannot release the hold. Manual pause is an independent switch. Next: Complete the build, release the correct hold and verify completion. Add a new dependency JAR to the JVM classpath Needs a restart The running JVM startup classpath is not replaced by watching class outputs. Next: Restart with the updated launch classpath. How request timing, build holds and pause interact

title: Default: immediate application
text: Default: immediate application The default reloadBoundary=immediate installs no request hook. A request can call old code, cross a reload, then call new code. This is the ordinary reload behavior; application-wide atomicity is not implied. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Opt in to a supported MVC request boundary
text: Opt in to a supported MVC request boundary shell java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=reloadBoundary=request" -jar app.jar Start with the agent before MVC loads. Supported requests finish before the class batch and framework follow-up run; new requests wait during application. The agent waits up to one second to drain active requests, then admits traffic again and retains the edit for a natural idle boundary. The one-second limit applies to draining, not total reload duration. A long framework follow-up can delay new requests for longer. An uncompleted async request or a Callable worker ignoring cancellation can defer reload indefinitely. Native Spring 5 javax / Spring 6 Jakarta MVC dispatches include supported Callable, WebAsyncTask and DeferredResult lifetimes through servlet completion. A timed-out Callable worker remains counted until its body actually exits. The boundary has a measured scope It covers successful method-body changes through supported MVC lifetimes. Filters outside dispatch, WebFlux, streaming/SSE, background jobs and arbitrary async work are outside that scope. Structural and partially failed batches retain their own limits. Recorded native graphs: Framework 5.3.39 / Tomcat 9.0.121 and Framework 6.1.14 / Tomcat 10.1.60, stock SapMachine 17/21, ordinary/child application loaders. A missing hook defers edits; it does not silently certify request protection. Use immediate mode for a non-MVC application. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A successful build controls admission
text: A successful build controls admission IntelliJ build signals hold class output while compilation is in progress. BUILD ok permits a complete captured batch only after success; a failed/cancelled build keeps it held. Newer build starts/failures invalidate an unfinished capture. SCAN does not release a build hold. Already accepted bytes may finish while the next build is held. AutoCompile stages all modules before publishing output. These controls protect admission; they do not make framework refresh transactional. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Pause is independent of build ownership
text: Pause is independent of build ownership The source baseline includes correlated RELOAD pause , resume and status commands. Wait for the acknowledgement; an old agent can ignore an unsupported command. Pause retains/coalesces newly observed work, but work already admitted can finish. Resume does not unlock an active/failed build hold. Its acknowledgement describes admission state, not completed reload. It does not freeze application requests, stop a classloader loading new disk output, or roll back changes. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A batch can apply partially
text: A batch can apply partially JVM redefinition, framework metadata, singleton lifecycle and external resources are not one transaction. A later step can fail after earlier changes are already live. Read the pending ledger and verify the actual behavior before calling the save complete. Saving the old source can reload the old implementation, but does not recover lost bean state, reverse DDL, undo imported data or restore consumed messages. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Still stuck?
text: Still stuck? Include the application and agent versions, runtime, framework, launch route, compile command, minimal edit and expected versus observed result. Remove credentials, private paths and identifying application data. Report a reproducible issue or read the security policy .

title: SAP Commerce
text: SAP Commerce In IntelliJ, open Settings → Tools → Reclazz. The SAP Commerce controls appear for a detected SAP project. Use its Install Agent action for server startup configuration. Application JVM argument -javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=autoImpex=false SAP Commerce options Option Default Behavior and scope hybrisHome auto-detect Absolute path to the hybris/ directory watchExtensions all custom Semicolon-separated extension names to watch (empty = all) autoCompile false Compile .java files internally instead of watching .class files autoImpex false Auto-import changed .impex files impexAllowRemove false Let auto-imported ImpEx files run REMOVE lines autoUpdateRunningSystem false After an items.xml change regenerates the models, run the schema-only Update Running System (add columns, no data, never drop) so a new attribute is live without a manual HAC click. A saved *-locales_<iso>.properties also writes the type, attribute and enumeration names it keys onto the types, as "Localize types" would for those keys only. Writes to the live database, so opt-in and dev-only backofficeConfigReset true After a module Backoffice config XML save, perform the native F4 cockpit-config reset without restarting. Resets UI-made configuration too; does not reset widgets. Set false to leave the save unapplied and use F4 manually. autoSolrReindex false After a SAP Commerce indexing provider/resolver reload, queue a bounded native update of its existing local Solr documents. Runs normal platform listeners and bookkeeping. Development only; see targeted reindexing

title: Opt-in behaviour
text: Opt-in behaviour In IntelliJ, open Settings → Tools → Reclazz for JPA refresh, static initialization and reload timing. Custom cache-owner rules use the startup argument. Application JVM argument -javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=jpaRefresh=false Opt-in behaviour options Option Default Behavior and scope jpaRefresh false Opt-in mapping rebuild. Existing fields require enhanced redefinition; new entities also work on stock JDKs, including supported Hibernate validate with a prepared schema. See scope resetStatics false Opt-in reset of changed, isolated pure initializers of existing static fields; eligible static finals are made non-final at first load. Requires startup preparation; aliases keep the old object. See Changed static initializers reloadBoundary immediate request waits for synchronous MVC dispatches and supported Spring 5 javax and Spring 6 Jakarta MVC async requests before applying a class reload batch; requires -javaagent at JVM startup. See Reload between requests refreshOwnersOnHelper (none) Opt-in helperFqn>owner1;owner2\|helper2>owner3 : after a helper class reloads, recreate the named Spring singleton cache-owner beans so a custom cache they hold is rebuilt through the fresh helper logic. Owners are recreated through the normal guarded bean-reload lifecycle; non-singletons, FactoryBeans and event-listener owners are declined. See Refreshing a custom cache after a helper reload

title: How to read a support claim
text: How to read a support claim Support labels are scoped outcomes Label Meaning How to use it Reloads The documented path supports the change within its stated shape. Read the conditions, then check your application result. Conditional An opt-in, special JVM, restricted adapter or follow-up action is needed. Meet the prerequisites before treating it as supported. Restart The described change cannot be completed by this reload path. Perform the named restart/schema/platform action. Unverified The current source registry lacks the required acceptance lane. Run a relevant acceptance test; do not assume success or failure. No reload The source intentionally applies no Reclazz change for this case. An unchanged definition can be a valid no-op; unknown file kinds belong to another pipeline. The project evidence registries make a finer distinction: watcher observations, component-only contracts, expected refusals, failed capabilities and unverified environments. A green characterization test for a refusal is not evidence that the feature reloads. Consult the original record for the exact verdict. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Named framework lanes are not a universal matrix
text: Named framework lanes are not a universal matrix Stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64 are the main recorded lanes. The source targets Java 17+, but other JVM vendors, operating systems, future JDKs and enhanced VMs need their own acceptance evidence. Framework support is feature-specific: Core and ordinary Spring records name their own loader/shape limits. Modern MVC callbacks and native request boundaries have explicit Spring 6.1.14 records. Messaging uses exact Kafka/JMS/Rabbit and broker combinations, listed in its guide. Current native Boot properties/YAML P5 evidence uses Boot 2.7.18, not a fresh complete Boot 3 matrix. File-template observers do not establish packaged-resource or full view integration. SDK-derived Spring graphs are not deployed SAP tenant or cluster acceptance. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Contribute a verified improvement
text: Contribute a verified improvement Open source under Apache 2.0, with separate trademark terms for the name and mark. Start with a minimal synthetic reproduction and an observable before/after result. For a new support claim, record version, operating system, JVM, classloader, attachment route and the exact supported/unsupported shapes. Keep tutorials, task guides, explanation and reference distinct. Put prerequisites before actions, keep example paths synthetic, and attach limitations to the claim they qualify. Update the support record and the relevant guide together. Contributing guide ↗ Support the project ↗

title: Development trust boundary
text: Development trust boundary Writing watched class output can execute code in the application JVM. Opt-in ImpEx/schema features can change the development database. Treat watch directories as trusted application inputs. The local socket binds to 127.0.0.1 and may expose class names and paths to other users who can reach it on the host. This documentation adds no analytics or remote search. Search runs in your browser against the site’s static index. External project links and the site’s existing font host are separate network requests. Read the technical reference ↗ Development trust context ↗

title: Installation
text: Choose the route that starts your application JVM . IntelliJ and SAP Commerce are optional; Reclazz also runs with Spring Boot and plain Java. How you run the application Start here IntelliJ Java run configuration Install and enable the IDE plugin Spring Boot with Gradle bootRun Gradle setup Plain Java with Gradle application / run Opt-in application run Spring Boot with Maven Maven development profile Plain Java, another IDE or a custom launcher Standalone agent SAP Commerce scripts or IntelliJ SAP Commerce setup An AI client should inspect the running app Optional MCP server , after one of the above Use one attachment route for a given JVM. Installing an IDE plugin, adding a Spring starter or connecting an MCP client is not by itself evidence of a reload. Finish with your first reload . Versions and requirements The agent and MCP server target Java 17+ . JDK 17/21 are the baseline test lanes; the client matrix records narrower OS/framework coverage. This is not a guarantee for every later JDK or framework version. JDK 25 runtime: unit, end-to-end and Spring 6 suites passed locally on macOS on 2026-11-14 , with Spring 5/6 process fixtures targeting Java 21. Gradle builds on JDK 21

title: Versions and requirements
text: Versions and requirements The agent and MCP server target Java 17+ . JDK 17/21 are the baseline test lanes; the client matrix records narrower OS/framework coverage. This is not a guarantee for every later JDK or framework version. JDK 25 runtime: unit, end-to-end and Spring 6 suites passed locally on macOS on 2026-11-14 , with Spring 5/6 process fixtures targeting Java 21. Gradle builds on JDK 21 and launches tests on 25. The Ubuntu/JDK25 CI lane is configured; Linux CI is pending . Spring 7 was exercised with application classes targeting 25, with two first- @Bean cases still in independent audit; this is not a full Spring 7/JDK25 pass. See the runtime matrix . The IDE plugin declares IntelliJ builds 233 through 262.* (2023.3–2026.2). IDE compatibility and application-JVM compatibility are separate. SAP Commerce is needed only for the SAP route; see its guide . Stock JDKs support Reclazz's documented structural reload paths; a special JBR installation is not required to begin. Supported changes and native type limits are in usage and superclass feasibility . Examples use source version 1.7.0 . A source version is not proof that every registry has published it. Choose a version present in your chosen channel or build from source . Match the agent and its integration artifacts; newer BUILD/VERIFY/MCP features may require local builds.

title: IntelliJ IDEA
text: IntelliJ IDEA Open Settings → Plugins → Marketplace , search for Reclazz , install it and restart the IDE if prompted. Alternatively, use Install Plugin from Disk… with a plugin ZIP from GitHub Releases . Choose a release that actually contains the ZIP; the agent JAR is not the IDE plugin. Open the project and enable Settings → Tools → Reclazz → Enable Reclazz . It is off by default. This also works for non-SAP projects. Start a Java run configuration handled by the IDE. Reclazz supplies its bundled agent and watches the IDE's module compiler outputs. For a run delegated to Gradle or Maven, follow the Gradle or Maven setup rather than assuming IDE injection. Compile a small edit with the build that writes those watched outputs, then check the running application's response. Detailed options: usage . The ZIP contains agent/reclazz-agent.jar under the plugin's installed root; that bundled name is deliberately unversioned. No separate agent download is needed for IDE-managed runs. SAP launches outside the IDE use a staged copy; follow the SAP guide rather than persisting a path inside an IDE installation. For IDE-managed launches, one existing Reclazz VM option is reused only when its jar path and options exactly match what the IDE would inject, after quote parsing. A different path/version/options or multiple Reclazz flags stop launch with a conflict message. Remove the manual Reclazz VM option to use IDE settings, or disable Reclazz under Settings → Tools → Reclazz to manage attachment yourself. Other Java agents are preserved. Recognition covers reclazz-agent.jar and reclazz-agent-<version>.jar (version starts with a digit, classifiers allowed). Renamed jars at other paths, environment-provided flags and @argfiles are not inspected; option order and equivalent filesystem paths are not normalized.

title: Optional command-line plugin installation
text: Optional command-line plugin installation JetBrains documents installPlugins for its launchers. These examples use the 2026.2 launcher documentation , not a fresh OS/IDE installation test. Adjust the IDE path/name to your installation; older IDE launchers need their own check. sh # macOS, standalone IntelliJ IDEA installation open -na "IntelliJ IDEA.app" --args installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz # Linux, example installation directory /opt/idea/bin/idea.sh installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz bat :: Windows cmd.exe, with the IDE bin directory on PATH idea64.exe installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz For Toolbox-managed IDEs, use the launcher name configured in Toolbox. These commands install the plugin only; still enable it for the project and start the application with the agent. See JetBrains' plugin installation and OS-specific launchers .

title: Gradle
text: Gradle For an existing Spring Boot application, retain its Spring Boot version and add the Reclazz plugin to its build.gradle.kts : kotlin plugins { id("com.onurkat.reclazz") version "1.7.0" } repositories { mavenCentral() } Start with ./gradlew bootRun (Windows: gradlew.bat bootRun ). In another terminal, compile edits with ./gradlew classes . The plugin attaches to bootRun and test JVMs. Plain application.run is opt-in with reclazz { applyToRun.set(true) } in a plugin build containing the new option; see the application run guide for its availability and scope. Automatic watching includes all main class outputs; an explicit watchDirs list replaces them in the Gradle options . If that plugin version is not available in the Plugin Portal, use a released matching version or the standalone route. A local agent can be selected via reclazz { agentJar.set(file("/absolute/path/to/agent-1.7.0.jar")) } ; this replaces agent resolution, not Gradle plugin resolution. Full setup: Gradle plugin .

title: Maven
text: Maven Use the opt-in reclazz-dev profile in the Maven guide . It attaches the agent to spring-boot:run while retaining your other JVM arguments: sh mvn -Preclazz-dev reclazz:prepare-agent spring-boot:run # In another terminal, in the same application directory: mvn compile A complete runnable Maven example includes the POM, endpoint, version selection and first-reload steps. Keep your application's existing Boot version; the example's Boot 3.3.5 pin is a reproducible fixture, not an upgrade recommendation. The longer dependency-plugin alternative remains in the Maven guide . The optional Spring Boot starter reports attachment and can expose Actuator status. It does not attach the agent and is unnecessary for the first reload. Keep it in development configuration if you choose it.

title: Standalone agent
text: Standalone agent Download reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar from the assets of your chosen GitHub release , or build from source . Replace X.Y.Z and the application paths. Keep the entire agent argument quoted when paths contain spaces. sh # macOS/Linux: compiled classes must be on this application's classpath java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=watchDirs=/absolute/app/target/classes" -cp "/absolute/app/target/classes" com.example.Main powershell # Windows PowerShell: adapt the main class and output directory java "-javaagent:C:/Tools/Reclazz/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=watchDirs=C:/Projects/app/target/classes" -cp "C:/Projects/app/target/classes" com.example.Main Add your normal dependency classpath/JVM options as needed; Windows classpath entries use ; instead of : . For an executable application JAR retain your normal -jar app.jar launch, while pointing watchDirs to the actual recompiled class output. Watching source files or merely rebuilding a JAR is not this recipe. The flag must be present at startup so classes are instrumented when loaded. The watcher defaults to a 30-second startup delay ; wait before your first edit. For a small standalone demo only, startupDelaySec=0 removes that wait. Agent arguments and framework-specific limits: usage .

title: SAP Commerce
text: SAP Commerce Follow SAP Commerce setup for the correct Hybris home, launcher properties and compile command, or manual setup . Enabling the IDE plugin does not modify an already-running external server JVM; start it once with the configured agent before attempting reloads. Keep the server-facing agent at a stable path, outside versioned IDE installation folders.

title: Optional MCP server
text: Optional MCP server First run the application with the agent using one of the routes above. Then follow MCP installation : build or obtain the matching standalone reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar , verify its checksum, and point the client's stdio configuration at its absolute path and a Java 17+ executable. Use an explicit application portFile in tool calls when the client's working directory is different. The MCP server connects to the application; it does not launch or instrument it. MCP assets/features described on main are not retroactively available in older releases. Client coverage .

title: Building from source
text: Building from source From the repository root, with its Gradle wrapper and JDK 17+: sh ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar ./gradlew buildPlugin # Optional, only if you need the MCP server: ./gradlew :mcp-server:mcpRelease On Windows use gradlew.bat in place of ./gradlew . For the current 1.7.0 source: Output Use agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar Standalone shaded agent; use this exact path in -javaagent for a local build build/distributions/reclazz-1.7.0.zip Local IDE plugin; install from disk mcp-server/build/distributions/mcp/reclazz-mcp-1.7.0.jar and .jar.sha256 Optional standalone MCP package Read pluginVersion in gradle.properties if building another version. agent-1.7.0-thin.jar is not the standalone package. The source build's agent-1.7.0.jar , GitHub's reclazz-agent-1.7.0.jar and the IDE's bundled reclazz-agent.jar are different names for their respective packaging contexts. For local Maven plugin/agent installation, see Maven local builds . These commands build local files; they do not publish a release.

title: Your first reload
text: Your first reload Start the application with the agent and confirm the target JVM is the one you intended. Connection alone only confirms connectivity. After the watcher starts, call an endpoint or method and record its response. Change a simple method's returned text, compile to a watched class output, then call it again without restarting . Expect the new text and the same JVM. For complete acceptance with matching agent/MCP builds, follow the Maven installation verification recipe from its baseline step before editing: confirm the intended JVM/version with DOCTOR, hash the compiled class, require a same-session applied VERIFY receipt, and check the changed response in the same JVM. A successful connection or compile alone never completes this check. If only connection succeeds, do not call installation accepted: check the agent was present at startup, the compiled output is watched, and the current change is supported. Troubleshooting . Validation scope for this guide: the Maven example and standalone launch were exercised on macOS arm64 with SapMachine 21; details are in the example . Windows/Linux commands, Marketplace installation, IDE launcher installation and a live SAP Commerce setup were not rerun for this change. Their references and existing coverage are separate from this local verification.

title: Usage manual
text: Reclazz supports four modes of operation. You can use them independently or combine them depending on your workflow. Choosing the Right Mode Scenario Recommended Mode Server runs from terminal ( ./hybrisserver.sh ) Manual Setup Server runs from IntelliJ, compile with ant build IntelliJ Auto + ant build Server runs from IntelliJ, want instant feedback IntelliJ Auto + AutoCompile Rapid iteration on single files Auto-Build on Idle Server already running without agent Attach to Running Server CI/CD or headless environments Manual Setup with standalone agent Option 2: IntelliJ Automatic Mode (Recommended) Use this option when you run the SAP Commerce server from IntelliJ IDEA using a Run/Debug configuration. title: Choosing the Right Mode
text: Choosing the Right Mode Scenario Recommended Mode Server runs from terminal ( ./hybrisserver.sh ) Manual Setup Server runs from IntelliJ, compile with ant build IntelliJ Auto + ant build Server runs from IntelliJ, want instant feedback IntelliJ Auto + AutoCompile Rapid iteration on single files Auto-Build on Idle Server already running without agent Attach to Running Server CI/CD or headless environments Manual Setup with standalone agent

title: Option 2: IntelliJ Automatic Mode (Recommended)
text: Option 2: IntelliJ Automatic Mode (Recommended) Use this option when you run the SAP Commerce server from IntelliJ IDEA using a Run/Debug configuration. The plugin handles everything automatically.

title: How It Works
text: How It Works When you launch a Run/Debug configuration in IntelliJ IDEA, the Reclazz plugin: Detects that the project is an SAP Commerce (Hybris) project Injects the -javaagent flag into the JVM arguments automatically Detects your JDK version (17 or 21) and whether you are using JetBrains Runtime Adds recommended JVM flags (e.g., -XX:+AllowEnhancedClassRedefinition for JBR) Connects to the agent after the server starts Watches for file changes and shows reload status in the IDE You do not need to edit any properties files or manage the agent JAR path.

title: Setup
text: Setup Enable the plugin: Settings > Tools > Reclazz > check Enable Reclazz That's it. Run your Hybris server from IntelliJ as usual.

title: Project settings and managed SAP startup
text: Project settings and managed SAP startup Settings > Tools > Reclazz stores agent choices per project. Changes reach the next IDE launch or dynamic attach. For a server started outside the IDE, use Install Agent or Reinstall to apply the current form and regenerate its managed startup block, then regenerate the server config and restart as the installation message describes. Control Default Scope Import ImpEx files on save Off SAP Commerce; imports a saved watched ImpEx file Allow REMOVE statements Off Available only when ImpEx import on save is on; permits live row deletion on save Reset Backoffice configuration on save On SAP Commerce; the native F4 reset, which also resets configuration made in the Backoffice UI. Off sends backofficeConfigReset=false Update the running system after items.xml changes Off SAP Commerce development only; opt-in schema additions and keyed localization writes to the live database Update Solr documents after a provider reloads Off SAP Commerce development only; bounded native updates with normal listeners/bookkeeping, no proof of field freshness Apply reloads Immediately At the next request boundary requires the agent at JVM startup; dynamic attach explicitly warns and applies immediately Reload added and removed members (Advanced) On Off limits reloads to method bodies Re-run changed static initializers (Advanced) Off Applies on the next launch; eligible static finals become non-final. Existing captured copies retain the old object Exclude classes (Advanced) Empty Semicolon-separated class-name globs the agent never instruments Ignore files (Advanced) Empty Semicolon-separated globs; matching changed files are not reloaded Pause Automatic Reload (Tools menu and the Reclazz tool window) holds automatic reload in the running agent. Saves made while paused are kept and applied on resume; the status bar shows Paused and the number of waiting changes until then. It is a session switch, not a stored setting, and an agent older than 1.4.0 does not answer it. Existing JPA refresh remains opt-in. Its scope includes new entities on stock JDKs with a prepared schema; existing field changes require enhanced redefinition. See the JPA scope . The installer regenerates only its marked block from Settings; manual edits inside it are overwritten. Unrelated JVM options outside the block are retained. An existing Reclazz agent outside the managed block or in another properties layer is refused with its file and line before writing; remove that manual option before installing through Settings. This also applies to normal and debug startup options. A failed verification restores the previous managed file rather than deleting a prior installation. A project without an optional config directory uses local.properties with its managed block excluded from base-value verification. The log retains the agent's raw INFO lines for Solr FINISHED, FINISHED_UNVERIFIED and FAILED outcomes. Unverified indexing outcomes receive bold amber warning emphasis; failed indexing outcomes use the IDE's error colour. Ordinary WARN lines share the visible warning style. Solr outcomes do not change the independent class reload counter or mean that a successful class reload was undone. Platform/home/watch-directory/port discovery remains automatic. Diagnostic platform , wrapOutput , transformDumpDir , verifyTransform , sessionLog and structured refreshOwnersOnHelper arguments remain manual expert options (see Agent Arguments ); the IDE does not expose fields for them. The custom port/file controls choose which agent the IDE connects to, while its own launches use an automatically assigned port and project port file.

title: Workflow with ant build
text: Workflow with ant build This is the default and safest workflow. The IntelliJ plugin injects the agent, but compilation is still handled by ant : text 1. Start the SAP Commerce server from IntelliJ (Run/Debug) └── Reclazz agent is automatically injected └── Plugin connects to the agent └── Status bar shows "Reclazz: Connected" 2. Edit your Java source files in IntelliJ 3. Compile with ant (from terminal or IntelliJ terminal): cd hybris/bin/platform ant build 4. Reclazz detects the new .class files and hot-swaps them └── Reclazz tool window shows reload details └── Status bar updates: "Reclazz: 1 reloads" 5. Test your changes immediately

title: Workflow with IntelliJ Build (AutoCompile mode)
text: Workflow with IntelliJ Build (AutoCompile mode) If you prefer to skip ant build entirely, enable AutoCompile . In this mode, Reclazz watches .java source files and compiles them internally using the JDK compiler API ( javax.tools ): Go to Settings > Tools > Reclazz Check AutoCompile (compile .java files internally instead of using ant) Start the server from IntelliJ text 1. Start the SAP Commerce server from IntelliJ (Run/Debug) └── Reclazz agent is injected with autoCompile=true 2. Edit a Java source file in IntelliJ 3. Save the file (Ctrl+S / Cmd+S) └── Reclazz detects the .java change └── Compiles it internally using javax.tools └── Hot-swaps the resulting bytecode └── "Compiled: MyService.java (45ms) → Hot-swapped: com.example.MyService (8ms)" 4. Test your changes immediately, no ant build, no server restart AutoCompile treats the sources collected in one attempt as a package. All modules compile into a temporary directory, in dependency order, before any output is published. If compilation fails, the output directories stay unchanged and the running classes keep their previous version. The log names the compiler error and the number of held source files. Fixing any source retries the held sources together with the new save. Deleting a blocking source removes it and retries the remaining sources. While one source is broken, other saves join its held package. Two saves collected in separate attempts are separate packages. This is not an editor-wide refactoring transaction. Use the normal build tool for generated code and resources that depend on build tasks or annotation-processor setup. Do not run AutoCompile and an external compiler against the same output tree at the same time. Each successful output file is replaced through a temporary file and rename. If publication fails partway through, no agent reload starts, but earlier replacements remain on disk. The error names the failed file; fixing the I/O problem and saving again retries the package. Class loaders can observe mixed old and new files during publication. Reload and framework operations still have their existing per-class failure behavior. For external builds, the IntelliJ plugin holds class changes from build start until successful compilation. Errors or cancellation keep them held until the next successful build. A lost connection never implies success. HEALTH reports the held count and time; a missing result produces a warning after five minutes. The BUILD protocol explains recovery and a Gradle/Maven wrapper. Without BUILD signals, the existing file-watching behavior continues.

title: What the Plugin Shows
text: What the Plugin Shows Status bar widget: Bottom-right corner shows connection status and reload count Reclazz: Idle , Plugin enabled, server not running Reclazz: Connected , Agent connected, watching for changes Reclazz: 5 reloads , Number of successful hot-swaps in this session Reclazz: Error , Last reload failed (check tool window for details) Tool window: Bottom panel labeled "Reclazz" shows a detailed log of all events: Compilation results (autoCompile mode) One line per reload, with the timing and what the save touched: Reloaded com.acme.OrderService (12ms): bean orderService re-created, mappings re-scanned, caches evicted . When the save added something that only a restart completes, the line ends with 1 thing now waits on a restart, ask PENDING . The same line is the status bar widget's tooltip. Each framework step's own sentence, under verbose=true Errors and warnings Export Log saves the latest 500 events received by this panel , oldest first in arrival order. This includes warnings, information, compilation and connection/disconnection events as well as reloads and errors. Each new event beyond the limit evicts the oldest, regardless of level; the export header states the retained count and limit. Export takes a consistent snapshot while new events arrive. This is in-memory history for the panel's lifetime, not a durable record of the whole session: it does not replay events from before the panel opened, the initial waiting/connection banner, or filtered heartbeats. Notifications: Balloon notifications for important events (JDK detection, connection status)

title: Option 1: Manual Setup
text: Option 1: Manual Setup Use this option when you run the SAP Commerce server outside of IntelliJ (e.g., from the terminal with ./hybrisserver.sh ) or when you want full control over JVM arguments.

title: How It Works
text: How It Works You add the -javaagent flag to your Hybris Tomcat configuration. The agent loads inside the SAP Commerce JVM, watches for compiled .class files, and hot-swaps them when you run ant build .

title: Setup
text: Setup Edit hybris/config/local.properties and add the agent to tomcat.javaoptions , preserving any existing options in that value: Any JDK 17+ (works for structural reloads too): properties tomcat.javaoptions=-javaagent:/path/to/reclazz-agent.jar=hybrisHome=/path/to/hybris Structural hot-reload (adding/removing methods and fields) works on any JDK 17+ via Reclazz's companion-class reloader, no extra JVM flags required. On standard JVMs, the new members live on a hidden nestmate and are reached through invokedynamic routed from hot-compiled callers; reflective access ( Class.getMethod(...) , ModelService ) is limited to members that existed at boot time. See Companion-class caveat below for details. JetBrains Runtime / DCEVM (full reflective visibility): properties tomcat.javaoptions=-javaagent:/path/to/reclazz-agent.jar=hybrisHome=/path/to/hybris -XX:+AllowEnhancedClassRedefinition Enhanced redefinition applies structural changes to the original Class object itself, so reflection and reflective caches see new members without restart. Tip: If you already have debug options configured, you can append the agent to tomcat.debugjavaoptions instead. This property is applied when you start the server in debug mode: properties tomcat.debugjavaoptions=-javaagent:/path/to/reclazz-agent.jar=hybrisHome=/path/to/hybris -Xdebug -Xnoagent -Xrunjdwp:transport=dt_socket,server=y,address=8000,suspend=n

title: Finding the Agent JAR Path
text: Finding the Agent JAR Path The location of reclazz-agent.jar depends on how you installed Reclazz: Installed via IntelliJ plugin: The agent JAR is bundled inside the plugin directory. You can find it at: text # macOS ~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/IntelliJIdea<version>/plugins/reclazz/agent/reclazz-agent.jar # Linux ~/.local/share/JetBrains/IntelliJIdea<version>/plugins/reclazz/agent/reclazz-agent.jar # Windows %APPDATA%\JetBrains\IntelliJIdea<version>\plugins\reclazz\agent\reclazz-agent.jar Downloaded from GitHub: Use the absolute path wherever you saved the JAR. Built from source: Use the absolute path to agent/build/libs/reclazz-agent.jar .

title: Agent Arguments
