A released plugin lacking this goal must first be rebuilt locally; this feature has not been published by the acceptance workflow. mcpJar , port , owner and a nonempty buildArguments list are required. reclazz.timeoutMs defaults to 5000 and limits acknowledgements, not compilation. mavenExecutable defaults to mvn ; set it explicitly for a wrapper or another installation. Arguments are separate argv entries, preserving spaces without a shell. Include child settings, profiles, -f , properties and repository options explicitly: outer CLI configuration is not automatically forwarded. The MCP jar is a local standalone artifact, not a new Maven plugin runtime dependency. The wrapper waits for an owned started acknowledgement before launching Maven, and for ok only after the entire selected reactor exits zero. Any compiler failure, including a later module failing after an earlier module wrote classes, keeps the hold. Ownership rejection, offline agent or missing acknowledgement fails the goal. Retain the owner printed by the wrapper and rerun the complete repaired build with that same owner; never share it across concurrent builders. Use VERIFY / reclazz_verify_batch afterwards: build success is not reload proof. Only synchronous child build outputs on the selected agent are covered. Outer configuration/extensions, external writers, unselected reactor modules and asynchronous child work are not covered. There is no rollback or atomicity claim. The API target is Maven 3.9.9; the real reactor acceptance is run with the installed Maven version and recorded in the handoff. Windows acceptance is separate.

title: Spring Boot starter
text: A starter that makes a Spring Boot app aware of Reclazz: it reports at startup whether the hot-reload agent is attached, gives the exact command to attach it when it is not, and, where the actuator is present, exposes a reclazz endpoint with live status. The coordinate is com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-spring-boot-starter . What it does not do It does not attach the agent. A -javaagent has to be on the command line when the JVM starts, and a starter runs after that, so nothing a dependency does can turn the agent on by itself. Attaching is the job of the Gradle plugin, the Maven plugin, or a plain flag; see gradle-plugin.md , maven.md and for-ai-agents.md . The starter is the Spring-native half: it tells you whether that worked and surfaces the status. Add it kotlin dependencies { developmentOnly("com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-spring-boot-starter:1.7.0") } developmentOnly keeps it out of the production jar, which is the right scope: it is a development aid. On Maven, use an optional or a dev-profile dependency. With the agent attached, the log at startup reads: text Reclazz hot-reload agent is attached. Edit code, recompile, and changes reload in place, no restart. Without it, the start

title: Add it
text: Add it kotlin dependencies { developmentOnly("com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-spring-boot-starter:1.7.0") } developmentOnly keeps it out of the production jar, which is the right scope: it is a development aid. On Maven, use an optional or a dev-profile dependency. With the agent attached, the log at startup reads: text Reclazz hot-reload agent is attached. Edit code, recompile, and changes reload in place, no restart. Without it, the starter says so and prints how to attach it, rather than staying silent while nothing reloads.

title: Configuration
text: Configuration All properties are under the reclazz prefix. Property Default Meaning reclazz.enabled true Master switch for the starter's auto-configuration reclazz.fail-on-missing-agent false Fail startup when the agent is not attached, instead of only warning reclazz.port (auto) Connect to this agent status port directly reclazz.port-file (auto) Path to the agent port file. By default the agent's own portFile argument, then .reclazz/agent.port under the SAP Commerce home or the working directory, then .idea/reclazz/agent.port reclazz.hybris-home (auto) SAP Commerce home, to locate its port file Scope it to development the usual Spring way, for example by keeping the dependency developmentOnly , or by setting reclazz.enabled per profile. Turning fail-on-missing-agent on in a dev profile makes a hot-reload run required there: the app refuses to start without the agent.

title: The actuator endpoint
text: The actuator endpoint When spring-boot-actuator is on the classpath, the starter registers a reclazz endpoint. Expose it like any other: properties management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=reclazz text GET /actuator/reclazz json { "attached": true, "agentFlag": "-javaagent:/.../reclazz-agent-1.7.0.jar=platform=spring", "agent": "1.7.0", "protocol": 1, "port": 52227, "health": ["Reloads: 3, failures: 0, median 12ms"] } When the agent is not attached it returns {"attached": false} . The endpoint reads the agent's loopback status socket and reaches nothing off the machine, the same promise the agent itself keeps.

title: How attachment is detected
text: How attachment is detected The starter reads this JVM's own startup arguments ( RuntimeMXBean.getInputArguments() ) and looks for a -javaagent that names the Reclazz agent. It asks the agent nothing and opens no socket for the check; the status socket is used only by the actuator endpoint, and only to loopback.

title: IntelliJ + coding agents
text: This page is for a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Aider and the like) working on a Spring Boot or SAP Commerce project. It tells you how to run that project with Reclazz so your code edits take effect in the running JVM without a restart, and how to confirm that they did. What Reclazz gives your edit-run loop Reclazz is a -javaagent that watches compiled class files and hot-swaps them into the running JVM in place. Supported edits keep the JVM running; object state depends on the reload route, and Spring may recreate affected beans. See reload support and the SAP scenarios tested live for the proven scope. It is free, open source, sends no telemetry, and needs no IDE: everything below is a shell command or a build-file edit, the two things an agent already does. Turn it on Pick the build you are in. Each path attaches the agent to the dev run and the test JVM, so a plain bootRun / mvn test runs against reloaded classes. It

title: Turn it on
text: Turn it on Pick the build you are in. Each path attaches the agent to the dev run and the test JVM, so a plain bootRun / mvn test runs against reloaded classes.

title: Gradle (plugin)
text: Gradle (plugin) kotlin plugins { id("org.springframework.boot") version "3.3.0" id("com.onurkat.reclazz") version "1.7.0" } The plugin resolves com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-agent from Maven Central and wires the flag into bootRun and Test . It is published on the Gradle Plugin Portal, so the id(...) version "1.7.0" form above resolves as-is. Details and options: gradle-plugin.md .

title: Maven
text: Maven No plugin is needed. Let the dependency plugin resolve the agent into a property and reference it from Surefire and spring-boot:run ; a prepare-agent plugin is available too. Both are in maven.md .

title: Any JVM (works everywhere today)
text: Any JVM (works everywhere today) The agent is on Maven Central as com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-agent . Resolve or download the jar, then attach it at startup: bash java -javaagent:/path/to/reclazz-agent.jar=platform=spring,watchDirs=build/classes/java/main -jar app.jar The flag must be present when the JVM starts; the agent only reloads classes it transformed at load time. Every argument is in usage.md .

title: Confirm it attached and verify a reload
text: Confirm it attached and verify a reload Start with the complete installation verification recipe : record the intended JVM, inspect DOCTOR, compile a real change, verify its exact class-file hash in the same session and check live behavior. The existing tools below supply different evidence; an attachment check is not a reload receipt. Gradle task, one JSON line: text ./gradlew reclazzStatus json {"attached":true,"agent":"1.7.0","protocol":1,"port":54123,"health":["Reloads: 3, failures: 0, median 12ms"]} {"attached":false,"reason":"..."} when nothing is running. See gradle-plugin.md . MCP server, if your client speaks MCP: use the matching packaged reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar . Call reclazz_doctor before the change, then reclazz_verify for the compiled class/hash; reclazz_status , reclazz_pending and reclazz_diagnose help inspect the running target. Setup and the tool table: mcp-server.md . To wait through MCP, call reclazz_await_reload with action:checkpoint before saving, then action:wait with its session/subscription/cursor and either the compiled binary className , or filePath plus exact ownerClassName . Pass the expected compiled sha256 when available. The tool combines a received owner event with same-session byte verification; it reports compile errors, reload refusal, restart-needed hierarchy changes, holds and timeouts without treating them as success. correlationScope:received_events , sourcePathConfirmed:false and editRevisionConfirmed:false are explicit: this is not proof of a particular full source path or source revision. Check the endpoint/test after applied . See the checkpoint and wait recipe . To inspect several edits, reuse that checkpoint with reclazz_events , passing its cursor as sinceCursor , then each page's nextCursor . Exact level, owner and filename filters apply to one event at a time; query file and owner views separately from the same checkpoint. Event rows always have reloadConfirmed:false , including rows typed reload . An evicted cursor is unavailable and requires a new checkpoint, not a silent history reset. See event pagination and limits . For failed-build protection, use the terminal build wrapper or acknowledged MCP build sequence with matching jars that support build receipts. Plain compile commands do not provide that barrier. The basic loop: edit code, recompile ( ./gradlew classes or mvn compile ), let the agent swap it, then hit the endpoint or run the test. If a change did not take, call reclazz_diagnose with className and the same explicit portFile , or inspect the logs. reclazz_pending lists what genuinely needs a restart (a changed superclass, a reordered enum). Restart only for those.

title: Drop-in AGENTS.md recipe
text: Drop-in AGENTS.md recipe Paste this into the target project's AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md , .cursorrules , whatever your setup reads) so the agent that works on that project keeps using the hot-reload loop instead of restarting on every change. Adjust the build commands to the project. markdown ## Hot reload with Reclazz This project runs with the Reclazz agent attached, so a running app picks up compiled changes without a restart. Prefer this loop over restarting. Run the app (agent attaches automatically): ./gradlew bootRun # Gradle, Reclazz plugin applied # or: mvn spring-boot:run # Maven, see the project's POM Apply a code change while it runs: 1. Edit the code. 2. Recompile with the configured Reclazz build wrapper around `./gradlew classes` or `mvn compile`. If using MCP, require acknowledged `reclazz_build started` before compilation, then send `ok` only on exit zero or `failed` otherwise. This requires an agent with build receipt support; stop if unconfirmed. 3. The agent hot-swaps the changed classes in place. Do not restart. 4. Verify each changed compiled class with `reclazz_verify`, passing className, its compiled file's lower-case SHA-256 as sha256, and the same agent address. Require status applied, matching hashes and the same sessionId. Poll with a bounded deadline; any other status is not proof of success. This requires matching agent/MCP jars with VERIFY support. Then exercise the endpoint or run the test. An attached status or rising reload count alone proves no edit. Restart only when Reclazz reports the change as pending (for example a changed superclass or a reordered enum). Check with `./gradlew reclazzStatus`, or the `reclazz_pending` MCP tool if configured. An empty pending list does not prove an edit applied. Require the exact-byte receipt and the behavior check above; consult the documented reload support and tested SAP scenarios for scope.

title: Why an agent can rely on this
text: Why an agent can rely on this Zero config: the flag alone works, no config file required. No telemetry, open source: nothing phones home, so a safety layer around the agent has nothing to block. Loopback only: MCP connects to the status socket on 127.0.0.1 and reaches nothing off the machine. Await retains bounded subscriptions to selected local targets. The shipped agent jar opens no client socket at all; its own tests enforce that.

title: Reproducing the packaged consumer workflow
text: Reproducing the packaged consumer workflow From a Reclazz source checkout with a JDK 17+ toolchain, run: sh ./gradlew :mcp-server:test --rerun --tests '*AgenticEndToEndTest' This test builds the current agent and MCP distribution, then creates a clean standalone Java consumer project in a temporary directory. It copies both jars to an installation path containing spaces, compiles with the real JDK javac , and attaches the agent at application startup. A separate java -jar MCP process receives actual JSON-RPC stdio requests throughout the scenario. The proof covers: Attached status, a successful source edit compiled through the packaged BuildMain , an exact-hash reclazz_verify receipt, and changed live behavior. An acknowledged MCP build hold across a two-stage compilation: the first javac writes a changed class, the second fails on invalid source. The partial output cannot change the running application during or after that failed build. A complete repaired build releasing the hold, with matching hash evidence and changed live behavior. A stale hash returns mismatch . The same application PID, startup identity, agent session and increasing counter on the existing service object across edits and recovery. The test uses only local artifacts and JDK tools, without a running IDE or registry download. It exercises the documented direct -javaagent route. It does not establish end-to-end coverage of Gradle/Maven plugin resolution, Spring Boot or a third-party MCP client's configuration. Those remain separate integration surfaces. The application, compiler, wrapper and MCP subprocesses have bounded waits and are cleaned up; their transcripts appear in the test report.

title: MCP for coding agents
text: Your coding agent can edit a Java service and finish a build. Reclazz's MCP tools help it answer the next questions: Which JVM is running? Were the changed bytes applied? Is something held or waiting for a restart? What should it check before telling you the change works? Keep the application running while the agent gathers that evidence. The bridge exposes eleven tools, read-only resources and a verification prompt through stdio, backed by the attached Reclazz agent's local status socket. Use the MCP reference for installation, full schemas and target selection. This page explains the developer benefits. Examples below come from recorded local acceptance through 10 November 2026 . Tool requests are shown as an MCP tool name and argument object, not a shell command. The resource and prompt examples identify their method and parameters. Results show selected fields or selected array entries, not complete responses. Uppercase session, cursor, path, hash and owner values are placeholders to replace with evidence from your own run. Rendering this page does not rerun acceptance. Find the right running application An agent can compile successfully while talking to the wrong server. Start

title: Find the right running application
text: Find the right running application An agent can compile successfully while talking to the wrong server. Start with reclazz_status for attachment and health, then reclazz_doctor for JVM identity, session, launch directory, capabilities and watcher evidence. json { "name": "reclazz_doctor", "arguments": { "timeoutMs": "1500" } } Recorded result excerpt: json { "status": "observed", "watcherState": "watching", "buildHold": "none", "verifySupported": true, "reloadConfirmed": false } Compare the returned PID, session and working directory with the application you intended. With an explicit project, the server checks that connection's DOCTOR launch-directory evidence before sending the requested command. Limit: Attachment and a healthy watcher do not prove that an edit reloaded. A sampled directory list can be incomplete; a working directory is not a repository-root assertion. See target checks .

title: Replace a guessed wait with a bounded result
text: Replace a guessed wait with a bounded result After saving, an agent needs more than a delay or an increasing reload counter. reclazz_await_reload creates a checkpoint before the edit, then waits for qualifying received events and an exact-owner byte receipt. First call reclazz_await_reload with action:"checkpoint" and require status:"ready" . Save only after that reply. Use its session, subscription and cursor in the wait: json { "name": "reclazz_await_reload", "arguments": { "action": "wait", "sessionId": "SESSION_FROM_CHECKPOINT", "subscriptionId": "STREAM_FROM_CHECKPOINT", "afterCursor": "CURSOR_FROM_CHECKPOINT", "filePath": "ABSOLUTE_SOURCE_PATH", "ownerClassName": "com.example.demo.HelloController", "timeoutMs": "10000" } } Recorded result excerpt: json { "status": "applied", "reloadConfirmed": true, "correlationScope": "received_events", "sourcePathConfirmed": false, "editRevisionConfirmed": false } Recorded acceptance also exercised compile_error , refused , restart_required and held , so an agent can branch on a failed compile, refusal, hierarchy limit or blocked admission. timeout and unavailable remain explicit outcomes, never success by silence. Limit: Received events do not identify an exact editor revision or full source path. A matching basename can be ambiguous. Require the explicit binary owner in file mode; read the receipt and still exercise the application. See checkpoint and wait .

title: Prove the compiled bytes before claiming completion
text: Prove the compiled bytes before claiming completion A successful compiler exit does not show which bytes the live JVM accepted. Hash the changed .class file and ask reclazz_verify for that binary class and SHA-256. Use reclazz_verify_batch for several class/hash pairs on one connection; inspect every result. json { "name": "reclazz_verify", "arguments": { "className": "com.example.demo.HelloController", "sha256": "SHA256_OF_YOUR_CLASS_FILE", "timeoutMs": "1500" } } Recorded result excerpt: json { "status": "applied", "className": "com.example.demo.HelloController", "detail": "method bodies" } Require isError:false , status:"applied" , the expected session and matching expected/observed hashes. A recorded batch result had allApplied:true while still reporting atomic:false and reloadConfirmed:false : its individual receipts are evidence, not an atomic application transaction. Limit: A byte receipt is not proof of the feature's behavior, source revision or successful database work. Make the HTTP, UI or application test the last step. See exact-byte verification .

title: Inspect several edits without reading a log by eye
text: Inspect several edits without reading a log by eye When an agent edits several files, reclazz_events gives it bounded, ordered pages from a checkpoint. Filter by level, exact owner or file basename to inspect the relevant observations. json { "name": "reclazz_events", "arguments": { "sessionId": "SESSION_FROM_CHECKPOINT", "subscriptionId": "STREAM_FROM_CHECKPOINT", "sinceCursor": "0", "limit": "100", "timeoutMs": "10000" } } Recorded result excerpt, showing the first two of eleven returned events: json { "status": "observed", "nextCursor": "11", "hasMore": false, "reloadConfirmed": false, "events": [ { "sequence": "1", "type": "compile", "fileBasename": "HelloController.java" }, { "sequence": "2", "type": "reload", "ownerClassName": "com.example.demo.HelloController" } ] } Feed back nextCursor to continue. Filters apply to each event together; an empty filtered page can advance over inspected nonmatches. Cursor eviction is reported as unavailable instead of returning a misleading partial history. Limit: This is bounded received-event history, not a durable attempt journal or a full-path/revision tracker. Event order does not prove an atomic batch. An observed reload is not confirmed application behavior; use await/VERIFY and your own application oracle. See event pages .

title: Keep partial builds out of the reload queue
text: Keep partial builds out of the reload queue A compiler can write some classes before failing on another file. Start an owned BUILD hold before compilation so that a failed build does not authorize that partial output. The same owner reports ok only after the complete build succeeds, or failed when it does not. json { "name": "reclazz_build", "arguments": { "state": "started", "owner": "YOUR_UNIQUE_BUILD_OWNER", "timeoutMs": "1500" } } Recorded result excerpt: json { "status": "acknowledged", "state": "started", "reloadConfirmed": false } The build hold also gates automatic source/resource reload actions. The live SAP acceptance retained the previous HTTP/class behavior under both started and failed holds, rejected a competing owner, then applied the latest source after the original owner's successful build. The terminal build wrapper manages these signals around the complete compile command. Limit: An acknowledgement is not reload completion. SCAN or resume cannot release the hold. Retain the owner token for recovery; do not send ok just to clear a warning. Already admitted work can finish, and framework refresh and external side effects are not transactional.

title: Stage changes while keeping the application available
text: Stage changes while keeping the application available Use reclazz_reload_control to pause automatic reload admission while preparing several edits. The application keeps serving requests. Resume when the changes are ready, then obtain receipts and check behavior. json { "name": "reclazz_reload_control", "arguments": { "action": "pause", "timeoutMs": "1500" } } Recorded result excerpt: json { "status": "acknowledged", "action": "pause", "paused": true, "buildHold": "none", "reloadConfirmed": false } action:"status" reads the current admission state; action:"resume" resumes it. Independent client acceptance checked held output, resume, exact-byte verification and changed behavior in the same application JVM. Limit: Pause does not freeze requests, roll back state or stop already admitted work. Resume does not unlock a failed BUILD hold. See pause and resume .

title: Give the agent a concrete next diagnostic
text: Give the agent a concrete next diagnostic An unchanged response should lead to an investigation, not another optimistic completion message. reclazz_pending exposes the restart ledger and admission state. reclazz_diagnose describes the last known outcome for a named class. json { "name": "reclazz_diagnose", "arguments": { "className": "com.example.demo.HelloController", "timeoutMs": "1500" } } Recorded result excerpt, selecting the actionable diagnostic line: json { "status": "observed", "className": "com.example.demo.HelloController", "complete": false, "lines": [ "Reclazz has not attempted a reload of this class, and the compiled file has not been rebuilt since this JVM started. The build did not reach it." ] } That result directs the agent back to compiler output rather than a server restart. A pending restart requirement calls for its specific recovery instead. Limit: Pending/diagnose use a legacy broadcast diagnostic stream with no response-end marker. complete:false is deliberate: the lines are observations, not a guaranteed complete or exclusively request-owned response. See diagnostic errors .

title: Use the same evidence loop for Spring Boot and SAP Commerce
text: Use the same evidence loop for Spring Boot and SAP Commerce The tools speak to the running Reclazz agent, so the workflow does not depend on an IDE. Recorded acceptance used both a Spring Boot sample and a clean, licensed SAP Commerce 2211 installation with synthetic fixtures. For example, reclazz_doctor returned status:"observed" and verifySupported:true on both targets. Applied byte receipts were followed by real HTTP assertions. Await acceptance exercised eighteen outcomes per target; event-page acceptance passed fifteen checks per target, including restored application baselines. These are recorded runs, not new runs of this page. Limit: Shared tools do not make every framework edit reloadable. Type-system updates, schema changes, framework refresh and restart requirements retain their own conditions. SAP events in this tool are not a dedicated SAP operation receipt API. See live SAP scope and reload limits .

title: Read SAP operation outcomes with their limits
text: Read SAP operation outcomes with their limits A coding agent investigating a resource edit can read a stable operation and outcome instead of interpreting every log sentence. Event pages and the event resource classify recognized ImpEx, codegen, items schema, Backoffice reset and Solr messages. Java await also includes a bounded list of recent SAP observations, so the agent can see related activity while checking Java bytes. This selected field projection comes from a recorded live ImpEx event: json { "type": "sap_operation", "sap": { "operation": "impex_import", "reportedOutcome": "applied", "reasonCode": "imported", "evidenceScope": "agent_message", "applicationBehaviorConfirmed": false, "resourceBasename": "test-data.impex" } } It is an agent message, not a request receipt . The row does not identify which edit caused it or confirm application behavior. Follow it with a native data or endpoint check. In particular, codegen generated precedes the need to verify applied classes, and Solr completion still carries fieldFreshnessConfirmed:false . Recorded live acceptance observed ImpEx applied/refused/skipped, codegen generated, items schema applied, Backoffice reset applied, and Solr finished/failed. Native data, generated classes/OCC, schema, stored documents and configuration media supplied separate behavioral checks. Other recognized outcomes have unit/fake-agent coverage only. Backoffice media checks do not establish browser rendering or widget/socket behavior. Limit: SAP observations cannot turn a Java await into success. Await keeps at most 16 SAP rows and reports truncation; invalid observation history clears them. Read the full typed contract and live coverage for outcome meanings and recovery boundaries.

title: Connect the coding client you use
text: Connect the coding client you use Claude Code and Codex CLI each discovered all eleven tools and made one real reclazz_status call against the Spring sample in recorded local acceptance: json { "name": "reclazz_status", "arguments": {} } Recorded result excerpt: json { "attached": true, "agent": "1.7.0", "protocol": 1 } Use the Claude Code setup , Codex TOML entry or Cursor configuration . The client matrix records exact versions, instrumentation and which configuration route was exercised. Limit: Cursor setup is documented, not verified. Its desktop installation did not provide an installed non-GUI Agent CLI for that acceptance. The two CLI results do not certify desktop GUIs, other operating systems or every tool in each client. Client permissions and provider authentication remain separate.

title: Read context and choose a verification workflow
text: Read context and choose a verification workflow A coding client may want attachment or restart context as a resource, or a reusable prompt before the next edit. reclazz://status and reclazz://pending provide the same diagnostic JSON as the corresponding tools. The event URI template shares the tools' existing checkpoint and bounded event history. For example, packaged SDK acceptance used these resources/read parameters: json { "uri": "reclazz://status" } Recorded attachment fields decoded from the resource's contents[0].text : json { "attached": true, "agent": "1.7.0", "protocol": 1 } This is a projection of the recorded result, not its port and full health data. Resource reads stay on the server's startup target; a URI cannot select another project or port. A successful read can contain unavailable evidence, so inspect its JSON before treating it as useful context. Clients can also retrieve verify_my_last_change through prompts/get : json { "name": "verify_my_last_change" } The prompt guides doctor -> checkpoint before a new edit -> real BUILD signals for external compilation -> await reload -> verify the bytes -> check the application. It explains already-saved edits and tells the agent never to send BUILD ok merely to clear a hold. Fetching the prompt executes none of those steps and grants no permission to perform them. Limit: The client decides how to surface these capabilities. Recorded Claude Code acceptance listed both resources and the prompt, but did not request the template, read a resource or retrieve the prompt in its constrained run. The official SDK separately exercised those operations. Event resources remain observations, not byte receipts, source-revision proof or application tests. Tools-only clients keep the same eleven tools. See resources and prompts for selectors, errors and exact client coverage.

title: Keep the Reclazz bridge local
text: Keep the Reclazz bridge local The transport is coding client ↔ stdio MCP server ↔ 127.0.0.1 status socket . The MCP server has no hosted endpoint or telemetry; the agent opens its status server on loopback and does not dial out. The bridge does not require a cloud account to contact the application. For example, the local status request above returned the agent's attachment and health. It did not need to upload source to a Reclazz service. The agent network guard checks built agent calls, while the bridge's socket client explicitly selects loopback. Limit: Your coding client can contact its model provider and send tool results there. Local Reclazz transport is not a claim that the whole AI workflow stays offline. Loopback is not authentication against other local processes. Mutating tools can trigger application callbacks and external side effects; inspect their conservative hints and require appropriate permissions.

title: Follow the proof, then check your application
text: Follow the proof, then check your application The documented behavior is present in matching locally built agent/MCP 1.5.0. Source presence does not establish that an older published release contains it; follow the matching-build instructions . Evidence area What was independently accepted Public contract or test Status, doctor, build, verify, batch, pause and diagnostics Local Spring/SAP tool probes and real application checks MCP reference , packaged workflow Automatic actions during BUILD holds Started/failed hold, same-owner recovery and restored SAP behavior Automatic action tests Await reload Received-event correlation, exact-owner receipts and negative outcomes Await tests Event pages Ordered pagination, exact filters, gaps and honest observation limits Event tests Resources and verification prompt Packaged resource/prompt contracts and SDK reads; installed Claude Code listing with explicit limits Resource and prompt reference Typed SAP observations Parsed messages from all five families, with separate native oracles and explicit unit-only outcomes Typed SAP contract Real coding clients Eleven-tool discovery and read-only status in Claude Code and Codex CLI Dated client acceptance The bridge provides tools, read-only resources and a verification prompt. SAP-specific operation receipts remain outside this work. No automatic restart, durable edit journal, source-revision proof or universal rollback is promised. Start with the setup reference , verify the intended JVM, and finish the edit loop with the application's own result.

title: MCP server reference
text: An MCP server that turns the running Reclazz agent into tools a coding agent can call: check whether Reclazz is attached, nudge a scan after a build, ask what still needs a restart, or diagnose why a class did not reload. Read-only resources expose the same status, pending and event queries, and a verification prompt guides the next authorized edit. It is a thin, loopback-only client of the agent's status socket and asks the agent nothing beyond its own state. It lives in :mcp-server , not the agent jar, because the agent's own tests forbid the shipped agent from opening a client socket. The client acceptance matrix records independent SDK, real build-tool and OS coverage, with runnable tests and explicit untested lanes. For the developer workflow, read MCP for coding agents: close the loop : each benefit has a recorded example and a limit, from target discovery to byte receipts. Running it The server requires Java 17 or newer and speaks JSON-RPC over stdio. It is a standalone jar containing its runtime dependencies; it does not need IntelliJ, Gradle or a separately installed Gson at runtime. Build and install locally From a source checkout, build matching agent/MCP jars and test t

title: Running it
text: Running it The server requires Java 17 or newer and speaks JSON-RPC over stdio. It is a standalone jar containing its runtime dependencies; it does not need IntelliJ, Gradle or a separately installed Gson at runtime.

title: Build and install locally
text: Build and install locally From a source checkout, build matching agent/MCP jars and test the MCP package: sh ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar :mcp-server:test :mcp-server:mcpRelease version=$(sed -n 's/^pluginVersion=//p' gradle.properties) install_dir="$HOME/.local/share/reclazz/$version" mkdir -p "$install_dir" cp "mcp-server/build/distributions/mcp/reclazz-mcp-$version.jar" \ "mcp-server/build/distributions/mcp/reclazz-mcp-$version.jar.sha256" "$install_dir/" (cd "$install_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c "reclazz-mcp-$version.jar.sha256") These are macOS/Linux shell commands; Linux can use sha256sum -c in place of shasum -a 256 -c . On Windows copy the same two files to a permanent directory and compare the SHA-256 from Get-FileHash with the first field of the sidecar (ignoring hex letter case). The sidecar names only the jar, so relocation is supported. Stop on a checksum mismatch. This stages/installs local files; it does not publish.

title: Release assets
text: Release assets The updated tag workflow will attach reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar and reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar.sha256 to future GitHub releases, next to the matching agent jar. This change is unreleased; it does not add MCP assets to existing releases. When a release contains these assets, download both from that same tag, put them together in a permanent directory and verify the checksum as above. Use matching agent and MCP builds for BUILD/VERIFY support. A checksum detects file corruption; it is not a signature or proof of publisher identity.

title: Configure a stdio client
text: Configure a stdio client For clients using an mcpServers JSON configuration, merge this entry into their existing configuration. Replace the example paths and X.Y.Z ; use the absolute path to your Java 17+ executable if the client cannot find java on its PATH: json { "mcpServers": { "reclazz": { "command": "/absolute/path/to/java", "args": ["-jar", "/absolute/path/to/reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar", "--project-dir", "/absolute/path/to/project"] } } } Keep each argument separate, even for paths with spaces. Do not include shell quotes inside the JSON strings. On Windows use escaped backslashes or forward slashes (for example C:/Tools/Reclazz/reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar ). Client-specific configuration file locations vary; this entry does not modify them automatically. Clients with another configuration format need the same executable and arguments. Restart/reconnect the MCP client after changing the entry. The application must separately run with the Reclazz agent attached. The --project-dir option makes startup independent of the client's working directory. Discovery checks only that directory's .reclazz/agent.port and .idea/reclazz/agent.port , in that order. For a custom port file, also add "--port-file", "relative/or/absolute/agent.port" to the argument array. The port file may be absent at startup; the application can create it later. An absent, unreadable, malformed or unreachable explicit target never causes fallback to a different file or project.

title: Claude Code
text: Claude Code From the project whose application will run with Reclazz, register the packaged server with Claude Code's project scope : sh claude mcp add --scope project --transport stdio reclazz -- \ "/absolute/path/to/java" -jar "/absolute/path/to/reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar" \ --project-dir "/absolute/path/to/project" Replace all three paths first. This creates or updates the project's .mcp.json . Inspect the existing file before merging an entry named reclazz ; do not overwrite other servers. The default local scope and the user scope instead store entries in ~/.claude.json . Project scope is not an installation of the Java agent; start the application separately. Reconnect Claude Code and approve the project MCP server if the client asks. Use /mcp to inspect the connection, then ask it to call reclazz_status with {} using only this server. For an isolated print-mode check, the installed CLI also supports --mcp-config /path/to/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config ; see the CLI reference . A configured server or a model's description of it is not proof that the call ran.

title: Codex
text: Codex Merge this table into ~/.codex/config.toml , preserving existing tables. Codex uses TOML MCP configuration , so the JSON mcpServers wrapper above is not a Codex configuration entry: toml [mcp_servers.reclazz] command = "/absolute/path/to/java" args = ["-jar", "/absolute/path/to/reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar", "--project-dir", "/absolute/path/to/project"] Replace the executable, jar and project paths. Keep each argument as one TOML string, including paths with spaces. Do not add a second table with the same name. This local stdio server needs no API key, HTTP URL or MCP OAuth login. The Codex client can separately require its own provider authentication. Restart/reconnect Codex, inspect /mcp , and request one reclazz_status call with {} . codex mcp list lists configuration; it does not prove tool discovery or execution. A temporary CLI verification can use explicit -c overrides and exec --ignore-user-config where the installed version supports them, without editing the user's persistent config. The matrix identifies which route was actually exercised.

title: Cursor
text: Cursor Create or merge the reclazz entry in the project's .cursor/mcp.json : json { "mcpServers": { "reclazz": { "type": "stdio", "command": "/absolute/path/to/java", "args": ["-jar", "/absolute/path/to/reclazz-mcp-X.Y.Z.jar", "--project-dir", "/absolute/path/to/project"] } } } Cursor's MCP guide also documents ~/.cursor/mcp.json for global configuration. Use the project file when this server should target only that project. Reconnect the server in Cursor's MCP settings, inspect its available tools and ask Agent to call reclazz_status with {} . Do not count a registered entry as a completed call. The separate Cursor Agent CLI has its own installation. If it is already installed, its documented agent mcp list-tools reclazz command lists tools; see Cursor CLI MCP . A desktop installation alone does not establish that CLI's availability. Some Cursor launchers automatically install or update it when cursor agent is invoked. Inspect availability before invoking that route during a no-install check.

title: Check the connection and target
text: Check the connection and target The current server exposes eleven tools, including reclazz_await_reload and reclazz_events . Compare the client's discovered tools with the table below. Then inspect the actual reclazz_status tool result, rather than the model's paraphrase. With a running, healthy target expect attached:true and health data. attached:false is an explicit diagnostic result, not a successful attachment. Even attached:true does not prove a reload or changed application behavior; use DOCTOR, exact-byte verification and an application check for that. If the client cannot start the server, check the absolute Java executable, Java version, readable packaged jar and its checksum. If it starts but cannot reach the application, check the selected project, the application's actual port file, and whether its launch directory satisfies the project check below. Client permission denial, missing provider authentication and an unreachable provider are separate from a server or target failure. Preserve the error and do not report an unexecuted tool call as verified. The client matrix records observed versions and unverified lanes.

title: Target selection and overrides
text: Target selection and overrides Startup accepts only --project-dir PATH , --port-file PATH , or --help . Unknown/duplicate options and missing/blank/invalid values fail before stdio starts (exit2, stderr only). The selected project must be an existing directory. Help writes usage to stderr and exits0. There is no shared configuration file, process search, parent-directory search or machine-global default. Relative startup project paths resolve from the MCP process's startup directory. A relative startup port file resolves from the selected project, or that startup directory when no project is selected. Each server keeps its own defaults. Per-tool selection works as follows: projectDir overrides the project for that call; relative values resolve from the startup project/directory. It resets the startup port-file default, so project-only overrides discover the new project's own files. Per-call port , then portFile , then hybrisHome take precedence over the startup port file. Relative portFile / hybrisHome paths use the effective project directory. An explicit hybrisHome uses only its .reclazz/agent.port ; absence does not fall back to the project/client directory. Overrides affect only that call. Invalid input does not retry against defaults. A call selecting another project's port must also select its projectDir when a startup project is configured. An explicit project opts into a launch-directory check: on the same agent connection, before the requested command, MCP requires a valid correlated DOCTOR result whose canonical absolute workingDirectory equals or is below that project. Missing/unsupported/malformed evidence, a relative working directory or another project's directory fails closed. This also applies to status and batch verification. It prevents a stale port pointing to an agent launched outside the selected tree from receiving BUILD/SCAN/reload commands. Working directory is not proof of repository root, watched-output coverage or which of two JVMs launched in the same project is intended. Inspect DOCTOR PID, session and watch evidence for those distinctions. If the application launches outside its project tree, use explicit --port-file alone (or per-call portFile ) without project selection; this selects an endpoint but does not validate its project. No-argument startup retains discovery within the startup working directory and has no project check. Old agents without DOCTOR cannot satisfy an explicit project check; use matching agent/MCP builds.

title: Smoke check without an attached application
text: Smoke check without an attached application Set MCP_JAR to the absolute installed jar path and run in a macOS/Linux shell: sh printf '%s\n' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05"}}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \ | java -jar "$MCP_JAR" Expect two JSON response lines: initialization reports reclazz-mcp and the jar's version; the tools list contains the eleven tools below. The notification has no response. EOF closes the server. If Java cannot open the jar, check the absolute path; if it cannot load its classes, use the packaged jar from build/distributions/mcp , not the plain development jar. A missing attached application is a separate condition: reclazz_status reports attached:false .

title: Tools
text: Tools Tool What it does reclazz_doctor Read correlated target JVM, session, live watch registration and capability evidence, with next checks reclazz_status Whether the agent is attached and how it is doing (reloads, failures, latency, watched directories), as JSON reclazz_build Signal started , ok or failed ; waits for the agent to acknowledge the signal, and returns a tool error if unconfirmed reclazz_verify_batch Read 1–32 unique class/hash pairs on one connection within a total timeout; cancellable through stdio reclazz_verify Structured exact-byte reload receipt; requires className and lower-case sha256 ; only status:applied is success reclazz_scan Wait for a correlated scan/enqueue receipt from the agent; reload completion remains separate reclazz_pending Restart-required changes plus manual-pause and pending counts reclazz_reload_control Pause/resume automatic reload admission or inspect its state; never releases BUILD holds reclazz_diagnose Why a given class did or did not reload last time (requires className ) reclazz_await_reload Checkpoint received events before saving, then wait for an exact-owner event and same-session byte receipt; reports errors, holds and bounded timeouts reclazz_events List bounded received-event pages from that checkpoint with exact filters; observations never confirm a reload Each tool accepts optional projectDir , portFile , port and hybrisHome arguments to locate the agent; reclazz_diagnose also requires className .

title: Tool execution errors
text: Tool execution errors reclazz_scan , reclazz_pending and reclazz_diagnose return isError:true with a text explanation when the agent cannot be reached or its handshake is invalid. Before sending a command, the client requires a JSON CONNECTED event with numeric status-socket version:1 and a nonblank string agent release. Malformed or unsupported handshakes do not terminate the MCP stdio session. Pending/diagnose also return a tool error if the connection fails, a diagnostic response is malformed, or no INFO answer arrives before disconnect/timeout. Silence does not mean nothing needs a restart or no diagnosis exists. An explicit empty-ledger answer from the agent remains a successful result. Invalid tool arguments still return a JSON-RPC error rather than a tool execution result. reclazz_status remains an attachment diagnostic: attached:false is a successful observation. If the handshake succeeds but health cannot be read, it reports attached:true with a reason describing the missing health data. SCAN has no acknowledgement in the status-socket protocol. Its isError:false means the command was written to a validated connection; acceptance and reload completion are unconfirmed. Use reclazz_verify for exact-byte reload evidence. The legacy pending/diagnose INFO stream is broadcast and has no request ID or end marker. Collected lines are diagnostic observations, not proof that the entire response was received or that every line belongs to this request.

title: Protocol version negotiation
text: Protocol version negotiation The server supports 2025-06-18 and 2024-11-05 . Send a nonblank string params.protocolVersion with initialize ; a missing, blank or non-string version returns JSON-RPC -32602 . Either supported requested version is returned unchanged. Any other nonblank version receives 2025-06-18 as the supported alternative; the server does not echo arbitrary versions. The selected version belongs to that stdio session. An invalid initialization request does not change it. Following the MCP version negotiation rule , a client that supports the returned version sends notifications/initialized and continues. A client that cannot support it should disconnect. This server advertises tools:{} , resources:{} and prompts:{} in both supported versions. Existing tool definitions and negotiated result formats are unchanged. Resource subscriptions and list-change notifications are not advertised. HTTP transport, sampling and elicitation are not implemented. Full initialization-order enforcement is not added here; for compatibility, direct calls before initialization retain the legacy format.

title: Structured tool contracts
text: Structured tool contracts Sessions negotiating 2025-06-18 receive outputSchema and annotations from tools/list . Every tool execution result, including isError:true , has a JSON object in structuredContent and the identical serialized JSON in its text content block. Invalid requests/arguments remain JSON-RPC errors without a tool result. Explicit 2024-11-05 sessions retain the existing text results and omit these newer fields. Tool Structured result reclazz_doctor status:observed with JVM/watch/capability evidence, or unavailable ; separate clientWorkingDirectory , nextActions , reloadConfirmed:false reclazz_reload_control status:acknowledged with action , paused , pending counts and buildHold , or unavailable ; reloadConfirmed:false reclazz_status Existing attached , optional agent , protocol , port , health , reason fields reclazz_scan status:queued or unavailable , enqueued on success, requestId , sessionId , detail , reloadConfirmed:false reclazz_build status:acknowledged or unavailable , requested state and owner , detail , reloadConfirmed:false reclazz_pending status:observed or unavailable , lines , detail , complete:false reclazz_diagnose Same diagnostic fields plus requested className reclazz_verify_batch status:applied , incomplete or unavailable ; ordered results , requestedCount , sessionId , allApplied , atomic:false , reloadConfirmed:false reclazz_verify Existing correlated receipt fields; status:applied alone is success, or the existing unavailable failure object reclazz_await_reload ready , applied , compile_error , refused , restart_required , held , timeout or unavailable ; explicit received-event correlation limits and a byte receipt for applied reclazz_events observed with ordered event pages, nextCursor , snapshotHead and hasMore , or unavailable ; always reloadConfirmed:false sent confirms a socket write, acknowledged confirms the BUILD signal, and observed describes collected diagnostic lines. None proves reload completion. The diagnostic complete:false reflects the lack of a response end marker in the broadcast stream. VERIFY preserves its exact-byte checks, and application behavior still needs its own test. Status, doctor, pending, diagnose, verify, verify-batch, await-reload and events advertise readOnlyHint:true and openWorldHint:false . Scan, build and reload-control advertise readOnlyHint:false , destructiveHint:true , idempotentHint:false and openWorldHint:true : live reload can replace behavior and invoke application callbacks with external effects. These conservative hints are metadata, not permission or safety proof. The schemas use JSON Schema 2020-12. The contract tests export real responses to mcp-server/build/tool-contract-fixtures . An independent check can be run with an existing Python jsonschema 4.x installation after the tests: sh ./gradlew :mcp-server:test --rerun python3 mcp-server/src/test/python/check_tool_contracts.py The Python checker validates the schemas, successful and failed results, and rejects deliberate missing fields, wrong types, invalid statuses and invented completion flags. It is an optional development check, not a runtime dependency.

title: Read-only resources
text: Read-only resources Clients can use resources/list to discover two fixed resources and resources/templates/list to discover one parameterized event resource: Name URI or URI template Data status reclazz://status Same JSON as reclazz_status , including attached:false and any diagnostic reason pending reclazz://pending Same JSON as reclazz_pending , including status , lines , detail and complete:false events reclazz://events/{session}/{subscription}?since={since}{&limit} Same bounded received-event page as reclazz_events , including unavailable reasons and non-proof flags All three use application/json . A resources/read result has one contents entry with uri , mimeType and JSON serialized in text . Parse that text to obtain the data object. A resource result has neither a tool isError flag nor structuredContent . A successful JSON-RPC read can therefore contain attached:false or status:"unavailable" ; inspect the data before proceeding. For example, these resources/read parameters were used in recorded packaged SDK acceptance: json { "uri": "reclazz://status" } Decoded contents[0].text , showing only the recorded attachment fields: json { "attached": true, "agent": "1.7.0", "protocol": 1 } The complete result also contains the target port and health observations. This excerpt is not an application-behavior or reload receipt.

title: Event resource selectors
text: Event resource selectors First obtain a reclazz_await_reload checkpoint with status:"ready" on this MCP server's startup target. Substitute its exact session, subscription and cursor into the template. For example, this is a parameter template, not a literal live identity: json { "uri": "reclazz://events/SESSION/SUBSCRIPTION?since=0&limit=50" } Use the returned checkpoint cursor instead of 0 when it differs. Each session and subscription segment accepts 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, _ or - . since is required: a nonnegative decimal cursor without leading zeros, fitting a Java long . limit is optional, defaults to 50 and accepts 1 to 100 without leading zeros. Query order can vary. The URI is limited to 4,096 Java characters; percent escapes, controls, fragments, userinfo, ports, extra path segments and duplicate, unknown or empty query values are rejected. Resource reads always use the server's startup target and the same existing checkpoint history as the tools. A URI cannot override projectDir , port , portFile , hybrisHome or a file path. Project evidence is checked as for the corresponding tool. No resource URI is fetched as a filesystem or network URL. A read does not create a checkpoint or reconnect a stale subscription. A checkpoint made with a different tool target override is not silently retargeted. Use nextCursor to continue through the shared history. Stale identities, future or evicted cursors, target mismatch and transport failures retain the existing unavailable event-page result; they do not become healthy empty pages. The default event-read deadline is 5,000 ms. Filters and a custom timeout remain available through reclazz_events , not the resource URI. Events still confirm neither applied bytes, source paths/revisions nor application behavior. Both discovery methods return one bounded page without nextCursor ; a continuation cursor is rejected. Listing them does not contact the agent. Event resource reads use the existing cancellable observation worker. Ping and pure tool/resource/prompt metadata remain responsive during that work; other execution receives busy rather than being queued. Status and pending retain their existing bounded synchronous socket behavior.

title: Verification prompt
text: Verification prompt prompts/list advertises one prompt, verify_my_last_change . Retrieve it using prompts/get with these parameters: json { "name": "verify_my_last_change" } The result contains a description and one fixed user message with text content. No arguments are accepted; an absent or empty arguments object is valid. Listing or retrieving the prompt performs no agent query, build, edit, model call or application action, and grants no additional permission. The prompt guides the agent through doctor identity checks, a checkpoint before a new authorized edit, the real external BUILD lifecycle where applicable, awaiting an exact-owner reload, exact-byte verification and the application's own HTTP/UI/database check. A previously saved edit cannot gain retroactive checkpoint or source-revision proof. BUILD ok is sent with the same owner only after the complete build succeeds, never just to clear a hold. Automatic agent compilation remains a separate path. Failed, held, refused, restart-required or unavailable results must be reported instead of an automatic resume or restart.

title: Resource and prompt errors
text: Resource and prompt errors Case JSON-RPC result Missing/wrongly typed parameters, malformed selectors, unknown fields, invalid prompt name or nonempty prompt arguments -32602 Well-formed unknown resource URI, such as reclazz://unknown -32002 Unexpected internal context-request failure -32603 Another execution while the observation worker is active -32000 Unsupported subscription or completion method -32601 New resource/prompt methods accept optional object _meta without interpreting it as a selector. No-ID notifications remain silent. A known resource with unavailable runtime evidence returns its diagnostic JSON, not an invented success or a resource-not-found error.

title: Recorded client coverage
text: Recorded client coverage Recorded locally on 2026-11-10 , with matching locally built agent/MCP 1.5.0: Client/check Observed Explicit limit Official TypeScript SDK 1.30.0, packaged real JVM Two resources, one template, prompt list/get; status, pending, observed and unavailable event reads Separate consumer acceptance, not an installed AI-client UI result Claude Code 2.1.321, constrained print run against temporary Spring sample Actual resources/list with both resources and prompts/list with the verification prompt resources/templates/list , resources/read and prompts/get were not requested with built-in tools disabled; no read/UI claim Independent protocol client against clean SAP Commerce Two resources, one template, status/pending read, prompt list/get and expected URI errors Protocol acceptance, not Claude Code or a new SAP operation receipt The client decides how resources/prompts appear. The earlier Codex/Claude eleven-tool acceptance and documented Cursor setup do not establish these new client lanes; see the dated client matrix . Executable contracts: resource tests , prompt tests and the packaged SDK acceptance . After :mcp-server:test , the optional independent JSON Schema check uses the same existing tool output schemas against actual resource data: sh python3 mcp-server/src/test/python/check_resource_contracts.py

title: Input validation
text: Input validation Each stdio line carries one JSON-RPC 2.0 object. Requests have a string method, a string or integer ID (not null), and optional object params. Notifications have no ID and receive no response. Batch arrays are not supported by this server. Malformed JSON returns -32700 , invalid request envelopes return -32600 , and invalid method/tool parameters return -32602 . When an ID cannot be determined, the error has id:null . The process continues reading subsequent lines. Frames are limited to 65,536 Java characters, excluding the newline; an oversized line is drained and rejected before the next line is read. Known tool arguments must be strings, at most 4,096 Java characters, without control characters. className for diagnose/verify must be a binary Java name of at most 256 characters (Unicode identifiers and $ inner classes are supported). timeoutMs is an integer string in 1–60,000, with defaults of 5,000 for build, verify, doctor, reload_control, verify_batch, await_reload and events, and 2,000 for status, scan, pending and diagnose. Paths with spaces are supported. Invalid numeric ports produce tool errors for scan/pending/diagnose; status reports them as attached:false . Diagnose rejects invalid names before connecting. The socket writer additionally rejects commands containing control characters or exceeding 512 Java characters, so a supplied name cannot insert a second line command.

title: What it does not do
text: What it does not do It opens one connection, to 127.0.0.1 , to the agent already running on this machine. It sends no telemetry and reaches nothing off the machine, the same promise the agent itself keeps.

title: Protecting terminal builds
text: Protecting terminal builds Build the current agent and MCP jars together from this source tree: ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar :mcp-server:shadowJar . This receipt protocol is new; it is not a promise that an older published agent supports it. Attach the built agent to your development app and use the resulting MCP jar as MCP_JAR below. From the consuming project's directory, wrap the whole compile command: sh java -cp "$MCP_JAR" com.onurkat.reclazz.mcp.BuildMain \ --port-file .reclazz/agent.port -- ./gradlew classes java -cp "$MCP_JAR" com.onurkat.reclazz.mcp.BuildMain \ --port-file .reclazz/agent.port -- mvn compile --port N selects an explicit loopback port instead. With neither option, the usual port files are located in the current directory. --timeout-ms N changes the receipt timeout (default 5000; range 1–60000). Command arguments after -- are passed directly, without a shell. Quote paths containing spaces. On Windows, use your command interpreter explicitly for .bat / .cmd build launchers. The wrapper generates a unique owner token and prints it to stderr before connecting. Retain that token: --owner TOKEN reuses it for recovery after a failed or disconnected build. Owner tokens are 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. A fresh token cannot take another outstanding hold. The wrapper waits for an owner-correlated started receipt before launching the command. It sends ok only after exit zero, and failed after a nonzero exit, launch failure or interruption. A lost connection is never replaced mid-build. A missing agent or missing start receipt prevents compilation; an unconfirmed finish returns nonzero. A confirmed finish preserves the command's exit code. The app keeps running. Class output from a failed build stays held until a subsequent successful build by the same owner. If the wrapper is killed, the installed hold stays in place. Run another complete wrapped build with the printed --owner TOKEN to recover; do not send ok merely to clear the warning. A lost ok receipt leaves an uncertain result, not proof that no reload occurred. Different named owners and unowned IDE commands cannot change an owned hold. A named start cannot take an active legacy hold. Ownership releases after successful output capture, asynchronously after the ok receipt. Lost owner tokens require an application/agent restart; no timeout or force unlock exists. Tokens identify cooperating builds; they are not authentication and cannot protect output from a compiler that bypasses the hold. Use a unique token for each independent build and retain it until recovery is complete. Use compile-only commands, not long-running bootRun / spring-boot:run . Normal unwrapped builds retain legacy behavior. The Gradle/Maven attachment plugins do not install this wrapper automatically. Receipt confirms the build signal, not completion of live reload; exercise the endpoint/test to verify behavior.

title: Protecting a build through MCP
text: Protecting a build through MCP For a client that launches its own compiler, call reclazz_build with {"state":"started","owner":"build-unique-id","portFile":"/absolute/path/.reclazz/agent.port"} and require isError:false before launching compilation. Afterwards call the same tool against the same running agent with the same owner and state:"ok" only for exit zero, or state:"failed" for failure/cancellation. Do not restart the app or run another builder between those calls. If the target changes, stop the sequence; the terminal wrapper is preferable when one persistent connection is required. reclazz_scan alone provides no failed-build protection and cannot release a hold. The MCP server signals states; it does not launch arbitrary build commands or place compiler output into its JSON-RPC stream. The caller must choose and retain a unique owner; it is required in both supported MCP protocol versions. Missing or malformed owner is an invalid argument. Ownership rejection or an old/wrong-owner receipt is a tool error. Use the retained owner for started, failed and successful recovery; a disconnected MCP call does not release it.

title: Verifying the compiled change
text: Verifying the compiled change For a concrete first installation, use the Maven verification recipe : it combines DOCTOR identity, class-file hashing, this receipt and an observable response, with next steps for wrong targets, stale sessions and unwatched output. Build and attach matching current agent/MCP jars; older published agents may not support this tool's socket command. After a successful protected compilation, compute SHA-256 of each changed .class file and call reclazz_verify with its binary name ( com.acme.OrderService , or com.acme.OrderService$Nested ), sha256 , and the same portFile / port used for the build. It returns JSON text with requestId, sessionId, className, expectedSha256, observedSha256, status, source, detail and completedAt. Request IDs are generated and checked by the MCP client. Require isError:false and status:"applied" , matching both hashes. All other states have isError:true : running , not_observed , mismatch , failed or unverified . Read the detail and poll with a bounded deadline for asynchronous completion; do not infer success from an increasing global counter. Connection, timeout and malformed-receipt failures return status:"unavailable" and isError:true . Bad input returns JSON-RPC invalid params. Optional string timeoutMs bounds each socket request (default 5000, range 1–60000). A fresh session ID invalidates assumptions from the earlier app. The receipt is bounded, latest-only evidence that the exact captured bytes finished the reload batch, including deferred refresh; it is not a build job ID or an atomic result for several classes. Warnings, ambiguous classloaders and never-loaded classes cannot produce a positive receipt. See the receipt contract . After verifying the relevant classes, exercise the live endpoint or test to prove the intended application behavior.

title: Check the target before an agentic build
text: Check the target before an agentic build Call reclazz_doctor using the same endpoint arguments as the other tools. Its default timeout is 5000 ms. The tool reads one correlated DOCTOR response and validates its types and bounds. Missing, old, malformed, oversized or uncorrelated responses produce isError:true , status:unavailable ; capability support remains unknown. Both supported MCP versions receive JSON text; 2025-06-18 also receives the identical object as structured content. Compare the target pid , workingDirectory and sessionId against the application intended for the build. clientWorkingDirectory belongs to the MCP process; neither directory is an inferred repository root. sessionId matches VERIFY for this agent instance. Capability booleans reflect installed handlers; observation can legitimately show incomplete startup. watcherState , live directory count, refused registration count and a bounded path sample expose watcher evidence. watchSampleTruncated:true means absence from the sample proves nothing about coverage. The sample can include source and resource watches too. Follow nextActions to inspect startup, output paths or a held build. buildHold reports only the kind of hold, never its owner token, and doctor cannot release it. Even a successful status:observed reports reloadConfirmed:false ; follow the owned-build, exact-byte VERIFY and application behavior checks for actual proof.

title: Bounded batch verification and cancellation
text: Bounded batch verification and cancellation reclazz_verify_batch takes items , an array of 1–32 objects containing only className and lower-case sha256 . Class names must be unique and follow the single-VERIFY rules. The complete array is validated before opening a connection. Endpoint arguments remain the same. timeoutMs is a string from 1 to 60000, default "5000" , covering connect, handshake and every receipt together. The tool composes existing VERIFY commands sequentially on one socket; it neither builds nor polls automatically. results preserves input order. Validated earlier receipts are retained when a timeout, disconnect, malformed receipt or changed session makes the remaining entries unavailable. It does not reconnect or combine proof from different agent sessions. Each socket reply is limited to 16384 characters, with at most 32 replies. sessionId is empty if none was validated. status:applied and allApplied:true require every individual receipt to be applied; incomplete means all receipts arrived but at least one was not applied. unavailable means one or more receipts could not be validated. Both latter cases return isError:true . Even all-applied is a sequence of point-in-time observations, not a transactional reload or guarantee that earlier receipts remain current. atomic and reloadConfirmed remain false. Test application behavior separately. Both supported MCP versions return JSON text; 2025-06-18 also returns the identical object as structured content with its output schema. The stdio server accepts one batch at a time with no queued work. While it is active, ping and tools/list remain responsive; other requests receive JSON-RPC error -32000 and can be retried after completion/cancellation. Duplicate active IDs are invalid. Initialization therefore cannot change a batch's negotiated output version while it runs. Existing non-batch tools retain synchronous behavior. For a pending batch, send a notification with the original request ID and no id : json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/cancelled","params":{"requestId":42,"reason":"No longer needed"}} Cancellation closes the batch socket, including during handshake or reply waits, and suppresses its response if cancellation wins the completion race. Numeric and string IDs are distinct. Unknown, completed and malformed cancellations are ignored. Await-reload uses this same worker and cancellation mechanism; initialize and other tools are not cancellable. End of stdin also cancels the active batch and frees its socket; keep stdin open while awaiting a batch result. Cancelling observation does not cancel application reload, undo changes, release a build hold or reclaim its owner. A result already sent may race with cancellation; clients should ignore such a late response, as described in the 2025-06-18 cancellation specification and its 2024-11-05 counterpart .

title: Build-plugin entrypoints
text: Build-plugin entrypoints The Gradle plugin's explicit reclazzSafeBuild task and Maven plugin's standalone safe-build goal reuse the local MCP jar's BuildMain for one owned connection around a complete child build. See Gradle safety and Maven safety . They do not change plain compile/build invocations, add automatic ok finalizers, or imply a published plugin release. Retain the owner for recovery and collect exact-byte VERIFY receipts separately after a successful build. A reproducible acceptance harness lives at scripts/test-build-plugin-safety.py . Build local agent/MCP/Gradle-plugin jars and package the Maven plugin, then run: text python3 scripts/test-build-plugin-safety.py --work-dir /tmp/reclazz-safety-proof --gradle /absolute/path/to/gradle It requires a fresh work directory, Java/Javac 17+, Gradle 8.10.2, Maven 3.9.x and an already populated offline Maven cache. --help lists explicit artifact and tool paths. It does not publish or install to the user's Maven repository; it uses a temporary cache overlay. Each tool exercises two real modules and a live agent: opt-out, partial failure, competing owner rejection, same-owner recovery, exact-byte receipts, up-to-date barriers and offline refusal before output. Logs and evidence.json stay in the work directory. A missing tool/dependency is a failed prerequisite, never a silently skipped success. Mac/Linux local results do not prove Windows compatibility.

title: Pause and resume automatic reload
text: Pause and resume automatic reload reclazz_reload_control accepts action: "pause" , "resume" or "status" and the same port / portFile endpoint options as other tools. For example: json {"name":"reclazz_reload_control","arguments":{"action":"pause","portFile":"/project/.reclazz/agent.port"}} Wait for status: "acknowledged" . The result reports paused , pendingClasses , pendingActions , and buildHold ( none , named , legacy ) as an admission-state snapshot. reloadConfirmed is always false. On unavailable , the action may have reached the agent; inspect status before retrying. Unsupported older agents time out instead of appearing successful. Pause retains observed class/source/resource changes; SCAN does not apply them. Resume schedules current output, but never clears an active or failed BUILD hold. A successful BUILD does not clear manual pause. Already admitted work may finish. The switch is shared by all clients of this agent, survives client disconnect, and is not a per-client ownership lock. Repeated pause/resume does not discard pending changes. See the socket contract for admission and count boundaries. No IDE control or automatic rollback is added.

title: Waiting for a reload
text: Waiting for a reload reclazz_await_reload keeps a bounded event subscription in this MCP process. Take a checkpoint before editing or compiling, retain the returned sessionId , subscriptionId and cursor , then wait on that same target: json {"name":"reclazz_await_reload","arguments":{"action":"checkpoint","timeoutMs":"5000"}} After saving, copy the returned identities into the wait call. The following identities are placeholders, not a receipt from a running application: json {"name":"reclazz_await_reload","arguments":{"action":"wait","sessionId":"returned-session","subscriptionId":"returned-subscription","afterCursor":"0","filePath":"/project/src/main/java/com/example/Service.java","ownerClassName":"com.example.Service","timeoutMs":"10000"}} Source mode accepts an absolute normalized .java path and requires an explicit ownerClassName to produce a useful result. Without the owner it returns unavailable with reasonCode:owner_required . It observes Compiled <basename> followed by an exact-owner reload, excluding inner-class-only events. The agent does not include the full source path in that compile event. Visible ambiguous same-basename sequences fail closed; this does not detect every path collision. Alternatively, select className instead of filePath / ownerClassName for externally compiled output. Class mode requires a new exact binary-owner reload event after the checkpoint, without inventing a COMPILE event. Both modes accept optional lower-case compiled-owner sha256 . Pass the expected compiled hash when available. Without it, the tool discovers the latest observed hash with one VERIFY query and checks that hash again; discovery alone never confirms a reload. hashSource:caller distinguishes supplied bytes from hashSource:receipt . Field or result Meaning correlationScope:received_events The cursor orders events received on this unbroken MCP subscription, not agent attempt starts sourcePathConfirmed:false The compile event cannot prove a full source path editRevisionConfirmed:false A previous in-flight attempt can finish after checkpoint; the tool does not prove an arbitrary source revision was compiled ready Checkpoint established; no reload is confirmed applied Exact-owner reload observed and a completed exact-byte VERIFY receipt validated in the same JVM session; reloadConfirmed:true compile_error A new compiler-error block names that source basename and line; bounded diagnostic lines retained refused Exact-owner hot-swap failure with a compatible failed byte receipt restart_required The observed owner reports a superclass change that was not applied; independently salvageable bodies may have changed held Agent-wide pause or BUILD hold observed; it does not prove this target was pending, and admitted work may finish timeout No qualifying evidence within the total deadline; never success unavailable Missing owner, lost/foreign cursor, changed session/target, malformed or contradictory receipt, or unavailable connection; inspect reasonCode Only ready and applied return isError:false . All outcomes carry the three correlation-limit fields above. applied proves a point-in-time completed byte receipt, not application behavior, source revision, atomic reload or retained bean state. Exercise the live endpoint/test afterward. Typed restart diagnosis currently recognizes the agent's superclass-change warning; unknown failures cannot become success through an unverified receipt. This is not an exhaustive classifier for SAP resource operations. BUILD ok acknowledges scheduling. A subsequent await can still report held before the agent accepts the queued build output. Reuse the same checkpoint and recheck after the caller's successful BUILD sequence; await never sends BUILD, SCAN, pause, resume, compilation or restart commands. Timeout covers the entire call, including connection, handshake, target checks and receipt queries, with the usual 5000ms default and 60000ms maximum. This MCP process retains at most two target subscriptions, each with at most 2,048 events and 1,048,576 retained Java characters. Returned diagnostics contain at most 16 lines of 512 characters, with diagnosticsTruncated when clipped. Old or evicted cursors return unavailable. A new connection has a new subscription identity even if the application session is unchanged; obtain a new checkpoint instead of silently reusing the old cursor. Await and events use the same bounded worker slot as verify-batch. Ping and tools/list remain available during a wait. Cancellation closes the observation socket, invalidates its cursor and suppresses a late response; it does not undo an application reload. A later checkpoint can connect again. EOF closes all MCP subscriptions, and idle target eviction never discards an active wait.

title: Inspecting a batch of events
text: Inspecting a batch of events Call reclazz_await_reload with action:checkpoint before editing. Keep that response's sessionId , subscriptionId and cursor . The read-only reclazz_events tool lists received observations from this same persistent subscription; it has no separate checkpoint action. json {"name":"reclazz_events","arguments":{"sessionId":"COPY_SESSION","subscriptionId":"COPY_SUBSCRIPTION","sinceCursor":"0","limit":"50"}} Replace sinceCursor with the checkpoint's cursor on the first call, then use each page's nextCursor . Reuse the same target arguments. Pages contain at most limit matching events, an integer string from 1 to 100 , default 50 . An empty healthy page returns immediately. timeoutMs is the total call budget, including target and session checks, default 5000 , maximum 60000 .
