Page field Meaning events Received events in ascending local sequence order nextCursor Last inspected event, including excluded events; feed it into the next sinceCursor snapshotHead Head captured together with this page's input history; later arrivals belong to subsequent queries hasMore Uninspected events remain through that head; they may not match your filters correlationScope:received_events Local receive order, not a durable agent history or attempt identifier sourcePathConfirmed:false , editRevisionConfirmed:false No full source path or source revision attribution reloadConfirmed:false Listing an event never validates an applied byte receipt or application behavior For example, if events 2 , 4 and 6 match and limit is 2 , page one returns 2 and 4 , with nextCursor:"4" . The next page can return 6 . A page with no matches still advances through its inspected snapshot. Reading the same input cursor again deliberately replays retained history; only traversal through nextCursor avoids duplicates. If you change filters after advancing, previously excluded events are not replayed. Keep an earlier valid cursor for another view. Optional filters are exact level , binary ownerClassName , and literal Java fileBasename , for example Service.java . Levels are INFO, OK, WARN, ERROR, COMPILE, RELOAD and STRUCTURAL_RELOAD. Filenames have no directory separators and are matched literally, without glob or regular-expression matching. Filters combine with AND on one event . A COMPILE usually has a filename but no owner; a RELOAD has an owner but no filename. Combining these filters does not link adjacent events. Query them separately from the same checkpoint when inspecting both kinds of evidence: json {"name":"reclazz_events","arguments":{"sessionId":"COPY_SESSION","subscriptionId":"COPY_SUBSCRIPTION","sinceCursor":"0","fileBasename":"Service.java"}} {"name":"reclazz_events","arguments":{"sessionId":"COPY_SESSION","subscriptionId":"COPY_SUBSCRIPTION","sinceCursor":"0","ownerClassName":"com.example.Service"}} Each row carries sequence , level , timestamp , message , messageTruncated and a parsed type . The timestamp comes from the agent's broadcast; missing or invalid timestamps are explicit null . Sequence orders rows even when clock times repeat or move backwards. Messages retain at most 512 Java characters, with messageTruncated:true when clipped. Parsing uses the full bounded received message, and optional filename/owner fields appear only when that event explicitly admits them. An inner-class display folded to Outer (inner class) cannot identify an exact binary owner. Types are compile , reload , structural_reload , compile_error , compiler_diagnostic , refused , framework_failure , restart_required , sap_operation and unknown . These describe emitted text; even reload confirms no completed receipt. A compiler diagnostic identifies a basename, not a full source path or a reconstructed compile batch. Unknown events remain visible. Known SAP producer messages have the typed observations described below; unrecognized messages remain unknown . Use await_reload / verify and an endpoint or application test to confirm a change. The two-target registry and each 2048-event/1,048,576-character ring are shared with await. Timestamp characters count toward retention. Evicted input cursors return unavailable/cursor_evicted ; future cursors return invalid_cursor . Disconnect, changed target/session, idle eviction or cancellation invalidates the subscription. The tool returns no partial page or advanced cursor on failure and never reconnects silently. Obtain an explicit new checkpoint; it cannot recover history lost before connection or after eviction. An unavailable result is a tool error, not a healthy empty page. Cancellation closes the shared stream, invalidating its await cursors too; ping and tools/list remain available during a blocked read. No BUILD, SCAN, pause, resume, compilation or restart command is sent by event listing.

title: Typed SAP operation observations
text: Typed SAP operation observations reclazz_events and the event resource expose recognized SAP messages as type:sap_operation with a nested sap object. Each row is an agent message, not a request receipt . Matching uses the complete received message and its level before display clipping. Unknown or malformed formats remain unknown . The nested fields operation , reportedOutcome and reasonCode describe that single message. Every SAP observation has evidenceScope:"agent_message" and applicationBehaviorConfirmed:false . Explicit resource basenames, counts or anonymous Solr target tags appear only where the message supplies them. Rows carry no operation request ID, edit revision or inferred link to adjacent events. Operation Recognized reported outcomes Observed live in recorded acceptance impex_import applied, refused, error, skipped, unavailable, warning applied, refused, skipped codegen generated, error generated items_schema applied, manual_required, unavailable, error applied backoffice_reset applied, disabled, error applied solr_reindex finished, finished_unverified, failed, skipped finished, failed The remaining outcomes have unit/fake-agent evidence only. Live acceptance used synthetic fixtures on a clean SAP Commerce installation: real ImpEx data checks, generated accessors and OCC responses, persisted schema/model checks, stored Solr document checks, and Backoffice configuration media changes. Profile restoration checks passed, followed by five default-suite runs on one boot and one on a fresh boot, each 46/46 with no failures or skips. These are recorded local acceptance results, not a claim that CI runs the native suite. Interpret the families separately: Codegen generated reports regeneration/compilation. Verify the generated owners' applied bytes and then exercise the application. Items warnings can report manual work or an unavailable automatic update; the shared warning cannot distinguish every underlying disabled/error cause. ImpEx warning/remove_allowed means importing with REMOVE allowed, not a refusal. Check the import result separately. Backoffice applied includes uiConfigurationReset:true ; it reports an F4 configuration reset. Browser rendering and widget/socket behavior require their own checks. Solr keeps finished_unverified distinct from finished . Every Solr row has fieldFreshnessConfirmed:false ; inspect actual stored documents. Mixed owner results remain separate observations, without an aggregate success. reclazz_await_reload adds sapOutcomes containing the latest at most 16 SAP rows after the supplied cursor, with sapOutcomesTruncated when older matching rows are omitted. The returned cursor comes from the same checked snapshot. Checkpoint results start empty; invalid history, session, target or transport clears the annotations. These rows do not select a SAP wait target or change Java await status: a SAP applied row alone cannot yield top-level applied or reloadConfirmed:true . Use event pages to inspect retained observations and the application's own tests to establish behavior. See the SAP observation benefit and the parser contract tests .

title: Scan completion support
text: Scan completion support reclazz_scan checks DOCTOR's additive scanCompletionSupported capability and waits on that same connection for its token/session-matched SCAN_RESULT. It returns queued only after file events were delivered to the agent callback. Zero is a valid unchanged scan; coalesced requests share a pass count. This neither clears BUILD/pause holds nor proves compilation or reload success. Unsupported older agents, missing/malformed receipts, session changes, stopped watchers, disconnects and timeouts return unavailable; no retry or reconnect silently turns an unknown result into success. Older IDE/wire clients retain bare SCAN behavior. Use matching agent/MCP versions for completion receipts.

title: SAP Commerce reference
text: This is the SAP Commerce (Hybris) counterpart of for-ai-agents.md : how a coding agent working on a Hybris project enables Reclazz from the shell, verifies it, and keeps its edit-run loop hot instead of restarting a server that takes minutes to come up. For the full human setup and every agent argument, see the manual setup in usage.md ; this page is the agent-oriented recipe on top of it. For application-level proof, see what we test live on SAP Commerce : 64 default scenarios, separate opt-in profiles, their repeatability and the areas that still need live acceptance. Why Hybris is different from Spring Boot A Spring Boot app is one JVM you start yourself, so a build plugin or a plain flag attaches the agent. A SAP Commerce server starts outside the IDE, through the Tanuki wrapper, and its tomcat/conf/wrapper.conf is generated: any -javaagent line added there by hand is wiped the next time ant regenerates the config, with no error. The supported seam is the platform's own append properties, tomcat.javaoptions and tomcat.debugjavaoptions , which are folded into the generated wrapper config. Write there and the agent is put back by the very regeneration that used to remove it. Enab

title: Why Hybris is different from Spring Boot
text: Why Hybris is different from Spring Boot A Spring Boot app is one JVM you start yourself, so a build plugin or a plain flag attaches the agent. A SAP Commerce server starts outside the IDE, through the Tanuki wrapper, and its tomcat/conf/wrapper.conf is generated: any -javaagent line added there by hand is wiped the next time ant regenerates the config, with no error. The supported seam is the platform's own append properties, tomcat.javaoptions and tomcat.debugjavaoptions , which are folded into the generated wrapper config. Write there and the agent is put back by the very regeneration that used to remove it.

title: Enable it from the shell
text: Enable it from the shell Get the agent jar. It is on Maven Central as com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-agent ; resolve or download reclazz-agent-1.7.0.jar and note its absolute path. Append the agent to the last properties layer your project reads, commonly ${HYBRIS_HOME}/config/local.properties . Append, do not replace: tomcat.debugjavaoptions normally carries the JDWP flags, and dropping those breaks debugging. properties tomcat.javaoptions=<your existing options> -javaagent:/abs/path/reclazz-agent.jar=platform=hybris,hybrisHome=${HYBRIS_HOME},autoCompile=true tomcat.debugjavaoptions=<your existing debug options> -javaagent:/abs/path/reclazz-agent.jar=platform=hybris,hybrisHome=${HYBRIS_HOME},autoCompile=true platform=hybris is optional (the agent infers it from hybrisHome ), but naming it is unambiguous. On JetBrains Runtime or DCEVM add -XX:+AllowEnhancedClassRedefinition after the flag for full structural reloads; on JDK 24 and newer add --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow so appending an enum constant keeps working (do not add it on a JDK older than 23: the launcher refuses to start). Regenerate the wrapper config and restart. This is not just a restart, the config has to be rebuilt from the properties first: bash cd ${HYBRIS_HOME}/bin/platform . ./setantenv.sh ant server ./hybrisserver.sh # or hybrisserver.sh debug for tomcat.debugjavaoptions The path in these lines is specific to this machine, so keep the change out of version control (a per-developer config layer or an untracked local.properties ).

title: Spring Security XML access rules
text: Spring Security XML access rules For a successfully observed local security XML file containing one security:http group, saving only its intercept-url access expressions can replace the served chain without restarting SAP Commerce. The candidate is built in a child context with the owning live context as parent; authentication services retain their existing identities. The servlet keeps its original FilterChainProxy , and only the exact owned chain slot changes. Other files' chains retain their order and identity. A failed candidate or proxy publication keeps the previous policy. Ownership comes from native namespace component events, not generated bean-name suffixes. Unobserved files, multiple http groups per file, matcher/route changes, authentication changes and other XML changes require restart. The focused native proof uses stateless HTTP Basic, an ant matcher and expression authorization; this does not claim OAuth, external identity-provider or method-security reload. Live Spring bean definitions and the native chain-list bean remain as booted. Consequently, getBean of a generated chain name still returns the boot object until restart. Reclazz separately records the parse currently served by the proxy so unchanged saves and repeated A→B→A edits compare with the active policy. The child stays open while served and is closed after replacement or owner shutdown.

title: Adding an ordinary XML bean with initialization
text: Adding an ordinary XML bean with initialization Append a new ordinary singleton bean to a Spring XML file already loaded by its owning context. Its class must already be visible there. Spring's native getBean performs InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet and an XML init-method ; Reclazz does not invoke those callbacks itself. An identical save retains the same initialized object. If native creation fails, its singleton and definition are removed so a corrected save can retry. This does not undo arbitrary external side effects performed by application callbacks. BeanPostProcessor, BeanFactoryPostProcessor, FactoryBean, SmartLifecycle, DisposableBean, destroy-method and non-plain construction remain unsupported for this path. Event-listener initialization retains the separate restrictions below. Existing lifecycle property edits retain their previous guards or recreation path. This does not add delivery of new Java classes or expand the default live suite. The focused SAP Commerce proof covers a precompiled InitializingBean and an existing consumer's lookup in the captured master request context; init-method is covered by focused Spring tests.

title: Updating a simple XML configuration placeholder
text: Updating a simple XML configuration placeholder A SAP Commerce property-file save can update an already-created plain singleton whose XML scalar property is exactly ${key} . The setter receives the current native Config value, with Spring's existing scalar conversion; the bean and its raw definition remain in place. A second change to the key updates the same bean. Only unchanged, successfully captured local XML and its actual owners are used. This path does not recreate beans, initialize lazy singletons or replay lifecycle, FactoryBean, infrastructure or listener registrations. Constructor/factory values, composite/default/nested placeholders, SpEL, collections and key deletion are outside this path. A setter failure names the key and bean in restart guidance; Config may already hold the new value. Native configuration acceptance is independent. A later save with no changed property values retries eligible placeholders from that file using native values, without storing pending keys. Setter side effects cannot be undone and setters should tolerate another invocation. No default-suite expansion is implied by the focused master-context proof.

title: Adding a plain XML event listener while running
text: Adding a plain XML event listener while running A newly added public class directly extending SAP Commerce's AbstractEventListener can be registered by saving a Spring XML file that was successfully loaded by the owning context. The class must already be visible to that context. Add a singleton bean with explicit tenantService and clusterService references to those existing native services. Spring performs its ordinary context injection, inherited initialization and listener registration; Reclazz does not add a second EventService registration. Saving the same XML again retains the listener and delivers each fresh event once. This path is deliberately limited to a class with an empty no-argument constructor, no fields or extra callbacks, and only its onEvent implementation (including the compiler's bridge). Custom constructors, lifecycle overrides, init/destroy methods, extra properties, application advice, parent/factory construction and changes to existing listeners retain restart guidance. A processor that returns a proxy is refused; failed creation removes the exact object registered by Spring, even if a later processor throws before getBean returns. Listener removal/re-addition and dependency/lifecycle changes are outside this path. Existing body-edit support is separate. The opt-in SDK regression uses the installed SDK without changing a running installation: bash python3 scripts/test-sap-events-xml-sdk.py "$HYBRIS_HOME" --agent /abs/path/reclazz-agent.jar Its tenant and cluster service proxies are isolated mechanics controls; real native delivery requires a live tenant. The native experiment uses genuine services and EventService delivery, with a restart-needing agent-off control and an identical-second-save check. It does not add a default live-suite scenario.

title: Persisted validation constraints after ImpEx
text: Persisted validation constraints after ImpEx The ImpEx watcher compares the persisted count and latest modification time of AbstractConstraint (including its subtypes) and ConstraintGroup before and after a finished import without errors. When either changes, it reloads the native validation engine once and reports why. Unrelated imports do not reload it. This is part of the watcher behavior; there is no separate refresh flag. The reload affects the service as a whole and is not atomic with concurrent validation requests. A reload failure keeps the successful import result and adds a pending validation-engine concern; a later successful reload clears that concern, leaving other pending reasons intact. Explicit modifiedtime writes can hide a constraint change; reload the engine manually. Same-tick changes that preserve both count and maximum time can be missed. A native query/service failure reports that refresh was skipped; the data import can still succeed. Check native validation and reload manually if needed.

title: The human one-click alternative
text: The human one-click alternative A developer in IntelliJ does not do any of the above by hand: with the Reclazz plugin installed, Tools > Reclazz writes exactly these properties into the right config layer (its own 99-reclazz.properties when an optional config directory exists), preserves existing values, adds the JDK flag only when the server's JDK needs it, and reminds you to run ant server . The shell recipe above is for an agent or a headless environment.

title: Verify it attached, and the edit-run loop
text: Verify it attached, and the edit-run loop The agent writes its status port to ${HYBRIS_HOME}/.reclazz/agent.port once the server is up. Check it machine-readably with the MCP server , pointing it at the Hybris home: reclazz_status with hybrisHome set reports attached, agent version and health. After ant build , reclazz_scan nudges a reload instead of waiting for the next poll; reclazz_pending lists what still needs a restart. The loop on Hybris: Edit a .java file in an extension. ant build (or let the IDE compile). The agent hot-swaps the changed classes. Exercise the endpoint or backoffice. Only restart for what reclazz_pending reports (a changed superclass, a reordered enum). Hybris-specific saves also reload without a restart: *-items.xml and *-beans.xml regenerate and reload their models and DTOs ( autoCompile=true ), changed properties and log levels reach the running server, .impex files import on save with autoImpex=true (a REMOVE header is refused), and interceptor registrations and backoffice labels are restored. A new items.xml attribute still needs its database column: by default Reclazz prints a reminder to run HAC > Update Running System , and with autoUpdateRunningSystem=true it runs that schema-only update itself (add columns, no data, never drop) so the attribute is live without the manual click. That option runs DDL on the live database, so it is opt-in and for development only. With it, a saved locales file also writes the names it keys onto the types (what Backoffice shows), only those keys rather than the whole "Localize types" step. A property added to a WsDTO shows in OCC responses after the regen. Business-process actions ( AbstractProceduralAction , AbstractSimpleDecisionAction ) are prototype-scoped beans the process engine resolves at each transition, so editing an action body takes effect on the next step with no restart: the next resolution is a fresh instance of the reloaded class. The same holds for a cronjob performable on its next run.

title: Drop-in AGENTS.md recipe
text: Drop-in AGENTS.md recipe Paste this into the Hybris project's AGENTS.md so the agent that works on it keeps using hot reload. Replace the paths with the project's own. markdown ## Hot reload with Reclazz (SAP Commerce) This project runs its SAP Commerce server with the Reclazz agent attached (wired into tomcat.javaoptions), so a running server picks up compiled changes without a restart. Prefer this loop over restarting: a restart costs minutes. Apply a Java change while the server runs: 1. Edit the code in the extension. 2. Rebuild: `cd ${HYBRIS_HOME}/bin/platform && ant build`. 3. The agent hot-swaps the changed classes. Do not restart. 4. Verify with the reclazz_status MCP tool (hybrisHome set), or check ${HYBRIS_HOME}/.reclazz/agent.port exists and the log shows the reload. For *-items.xml / *-beans.xml changes the agent regenerates and reloads the models; a genuinely new attribute needs HAC > Update Running System for its column. Restart only for what reclazz_pending reports (changed superclass, reordered enum). If the agent is not attached, it was added to tomcat.javaoptions and needs `ant server` then a server restart to take effect.

title: Opt-in new item type
text: Opt-in new item type With autoUpdateRunningSystem=true , Reclazz picks up one new generate=true item type live through native generation and the schema-only update. The items-new-type-attempt profile proves the generated Model and Jalo, deployment 31992/table, typed create/save, detached requery and a separate committed JDBC read without replacing the running JVM. This covers existing behavior. Run the outer driver scripts/test-sap-items-live.py --new-item-type --runs 1 with --fixture-manifest <reviewed JSON path-to-SHA256 manifest> , --restore-repo <normal checkout> and --lock <collab installation lock> . Select the disposable install with RECLAZZ_SAP_HOME and RECLAZZ_SAP_BASE . The manifest contains the exact normal fixture source membership from the shared suite contract, including any reviewed edits. The mode takes eight complete stopped snapshots, including concrete generated Jalo sources, and restores the database, config, bootstrap, native outputs, fixtures, original agent and links. It then proves the new type/table/classes absent in a fresh normal boot. Inner PASS with failed recovery is FAIL. Never run the inner profile alone or undo its XML on a live server. Native HAC credentials are read only from the disposable install's local config; the recovery checks use read-only native metadata and class observations. Default suite membership is unchanged by this mode. This bounded profile does not certify enums, relations, incompatible edits or arbitrary schema changes. No new dependency or production agent change is involved. The pre-generation negative control inspects class resources rather than trying to load a nonexistent class: SAP's enabled CacheClassNotFoundRule remembers failed class loads. After generation the profile requires the real generated Model/Jalo classes and rejects generic fallbacks. A class previously requested and negatively cached before generation is outside this bounded coverage.

title: Opt-in new relations
text: Opt-in new relations With autoUpdateRunningSystem=true , the existing native generation/schema path supports the bounded one-to-many and many-to-many relation edit exercised here. items-new-relation-attempt first creates two isolated generated endpoint types, warms their model classes, then adds both relations in one XML save. It requires new typed accessors on those same loaded classes and persisted asymmetric links re-read detached from both ends in a separate request. The one-to-many qualifier is relationParent ; owner is inherited from SAP's base Item and is not a new relation attribute. The many-to-many relation has its own deployment31995. Run scripts/test-sap-items-live.py --new-relation --runs 1 with the same explicit --fixture-manifest , --restore-repo and --lock arguments as the new-item-type mode. Set RECLAZZ_SAP_HOME and RECLAZZ_SAP_BASE to the disposable installation. The eight-root stopped recovery is shared: database, generated sources/classes, config and native outputs, original agent and extension links must all recover, then experimental types/tables/resources must be absent after a fresh normal boot. An inner PASS alone cannot pass the outer profile. Never run this inner profile directly or undo schema changes live. Future classes are inspected by resource lookup before generation to avoid seeding SAP's negative class cache. This opt-in proof covers existing behavior and leaves default suite and normal fixture membership unchanged. It does not certify arbitrary, localized, ordered, cascading or incompatible relation edits. No production agent change or new dependency is involved. Source membership comes from the shared suite contract; do not copy a historical fixture/test count into new profile checks.

title: Existing hot-folder converter references
text: Existing hot-folder converter references Changing the converter reference of an existing DefaultConverterMapping in captured Spring XML refreshes the native ImpexTransformerTask cache for that owner. Both referenced DefaultImpexConverter beans must already be plain local singletons, with an unchanged literal mapping prefix. Reclazz initializes a detached native task and publishes its completed cache to the held task, retaining the task and any static SingletonTargetSource proxy. Failed preparation restores that owner's previous reference and cache; it does not retry initialization on the live task. The focused live proof used real native file ingestion, conversion, import and cleanup: the reference edit produced the B row once, and an identical save followed by another fresh file also produced B once in the same JVM. Without the agent, the same edit kept using A. This proof is opt-in and does not expand the default suite or certify the whole hot-folder configuration surface. New/removed mappings, prefix edits, custom or lazy mappings, proxy converters, dynamic task proxies and unverifiable collectors require a restart. This does not reprocess a file already in flight or provide a transaction across tenants. The local regression scripts/test-sap-hotfolder-sdk.py uses installed SDK sources and proves native converter selection and row output; its standalone JVM does not prove tenant activation, CSV import or database persistence.

title: Existing file inbound adapter regex and rate
text: Existing file inbound adapter regex and rate In captured Spring XML, an existing explicit-id standard file:inbound-channel-adapter can accept literal filename-regex and positive millisecond fixed-rate edits. Reclazz prepares the new pattern and trigger, stops that adapter, updates the native objects and restarts it only if it was running. The source, scanner, composite filter and AcceptOnce history remain in place, so an already accepted file left in the input directory is not delivered again. Failed preparation leaves the old adapter untouched; a failed start restores the old pattern, trigger, raw settings and running state. This boundary requires the standard default file scanner/filter chain, no custom poller settings, and max-messages-per-poll="1" . Directory, filename-pattern, fixed-delay, initial-delay, custom source/filter/scanner/scheduler, executor, advice/transaction settings, added/removed adapters and nonliteral settings still require restart. Generated filter/trigger names are matched through the explicit adapter's own references, including when other XML files were loaded first. There is no promise to reverse a file delivery already in flight or to reprocess queued files. The default live suite and fixture membership are unchanged. The focused SAP Commerce proof measured the two edits separately in the same JVM: after changing A to B, fresh A/B files yielded counts [0, 1] , and the fixed-rate edit changed receipt gaps from about 2000 ms to 497–499 ms. The agent-off control kept A and about 2000 ms. The complete stopped twelve-root setup recovered and normal master/junit health passed. This proof used the literal A/B patterns; inline regex flags are covered by the local real-Spring regression, not a further live retry.

Structural hot-reload works on standard JVMs (SapMachine, OpenJDK, Temurin, Corretto…) via Reclazz's companion-class reloader, and on JBR/DCEVM via enhanced redefinition. Project configured and ant all completed successfully

title: Verify

title: 2. Hybris Project Detection
text: 2. Hybris Project Detection Open your SAP Commerce project in IntelliJ Wait for project indexing to complete

title: Verify
text: Verify Notification balloon: "SAP Commerce project detected" View → Tool Windows → Reclazz is available Check IDE log ( Help → Show Log in Explorer ) for: text Reclazz: Detected Hybris home at /path/to/hybris Reclazz: JDK detection, version=17, isJBR=true/false

title: 3. JDK Detection
text: 3. JDK Detection

title: Test with Standard OpenJDK (including SapMachine)
text: Test with Standard OpenJDK (including SapMachine) Set project SDK to OpenJDK / SapMachine / Temurin / Corretto 17 or 21 Check Reclazz tool window log Expected : Detected JDK 21 (SapMachine), structural hot-reload enabled (companion-class mode) The notification also mentions the one caveat of companion mode: reflective caches (e.g. Hybris ModelService ) won't see newly added members until server restart, because Class.getMethod(...) on the original class can't reach the hidden companion nestmate.

title: Test with JetBrains Runtime
text: Test with JetBrains Runtime Set project SDK to JBR 17 or 21 Check Reclazz tool window log Expected : Detected JDK 21 (JetBrains Runtime), structural hot-reload enabled (enhanced redefinition) Enhanced redefinition does not have the reflective-visibility caveat; new members are applied to the original Class object directly.

title: 4. Agent Injection
text: 4. Agent Injection Enable Reclazz: Settings → Tools → Reclazz → Enable Create or edit a Run Configuration for Hybris server Run the server

title: Verify
text: Verify In the console output, look for: text [Reclazz] Agent initialized [Reclazz] Hybris home: /path/to/hybris [Reclazz] Watching N directories for changes [Reclazz] Status server listening on port XXXXX Check .idea/reclazz/agent.port file exists Run Configuration VM options should contain -javaagent:.../reclazz-agent.jar=...

title: Verify

title: 6. Hot-Reload: Method Body Change
text: 6. Hot-Reload: Method Body Change This tests the most common scenario, changing method logic. Find a simple service class in your custom extension, e.g.: java public class MyService { public String getMessage() { return "Hello"; } } Change the return value: java return "Hello World"; Compile the project: Build → Build Project (Ctrl+F9) Wait for the .class file to be picked up by the file watcher

title: Verify
text: Verify Tool window shows: Hot-swapped: com.example.MyService (XXms) Status bar reload count increments: Reclazz: 1 reloads Calling the service in HAC or via API returns the new value

title: 7. Hot-Reload: Spring Bean Refresh
text: 7. Hot-Reload: Spring Bean Refresh Modify a Spring-managed @Service or bean defined in XML Change a method body and compile

title: Verify
text: Verify Tool window shows: text Reloaded com.example.MyService (XXms): bean myService re-created New singleton instance is created with updated logic Note: existing injected references still point to old instance

title: 8. Hot-Reload: Structural Change (any JDK 17+)
text: 8. Hot-Reload: Structural Change (any JDK 17+) Works on any JDK 17+, standard or enhanced-redefinition. Add a new method or field to an existing class: java private String newField; public String getNewMethod() { return "new"; } Compile

title: Verify (any JDK 17+)
text: Verify (any JDK 17+) Tool window shows: Structural reload: com.example.MyClass (XXms) New method/field is callable/readable from other hot-compiled code that calls it directly (via invokedynamic routed through the companion nestmate)

title: Reflective-visibility caveat (standard JVMs only)
text: Reflective-visibility caveat (standard JVMs only) On standard JVMs (companion-class mode), the new members live on a hidden nestmate rather than on the original Class object. This means: Class.getMethod("getNewMethod") on the original class still throws NoSuchMethodException until server restart Reflective caches (Hybris ModelService , Jackson, Gson, etc.) built from the original class at boot time also won't see the new members Jalo-layer property access and flexible search (which go through the type dictionary rather than Java reflection) do see the new members after a HAC updatesystem for Hybris items.xml attributes On JBR/DCEVM with -XX:+AllowEnhancedClassRedefinition , the original Class object itself gains the new members, so reflection and reflective caches work without restart.

title: 9. Interceptor Reload
text: 9. Interceptor Reload Modify an interceptor class (implements Interceptor<T> ) Compile

title: Verify
text: Verify Run the integration InterceptorReloadTest : it POSTs a unique nonce to /reclazztest/v2/test/interceptor-save , which calls modelService.save on a test product and always rolls back its transaction. Require HTTP 200 and validated-v2:reclazz-probe-<nonce>|calls=1 . A reload event, stale value, none , duplicate invocation or HTTP failure is not evidence of success. The fixture requires its own transaction and a test-only Commerce environment. A portable SDK registry check is also available via scripts/test-sap-sdk.py ; it does not replace the live model-save test.

title: Isolated OCC field mapping acceptance
text: Isolated OCC field mapping acceptance With an installed SAP Commerce SDK, run: bash ./gradlew :agent:compileJava python3 scripts/test-sap-occ-sdk.py /path/to/hybris The runner compiles synthetic DTOs against the local SDK, uses real XML reload, DefaultDataMapper and a Spring cache proxy, and checks BASIC/DEFAULT/FULL field additions/removals, repeated saves, parent/child visibility, merged declarations, unrelated contexts/caches and custom-helper restart reporting. It never starts SAP, contacts a database or writes the SDK. The SDK jars are not distributed. Add --disable-refresh for a negative control in a temporary compiled copy; this must fail on stale mapping output. This is an isolated SDK check, not live OCC HTTP acceptance. Use a JDK compatible with the installed SDK.

title: Isolated SAP list-directive diagnostics
text: Isolated SAP list-directive diagnostics After ./gradlew :agent:compileJava , run python3 scripts/test-sap-directives-sdk.py /path/to/hybris with an installed SDK containing compiled platformservices/classes . The synthetic fixture uses real SDK processors and converter output to verify restart diagnostics, unchanged live definitions/lists, repeated saves, inherited/subclass/lazy directives, shared targets, and unrelated XML property updates. Add --disable-guard to remove the guard in a temporary compiled copy: the restart assertion must fail. The runner neither starts SAP nor writes the SDK; it is not live application acceptance.

title: Isolated OCC request mapping acceptance
text: Isolated OCC request mapping acceptance After ./gradlew :agent:compileJava , run: bash python3 scripts/test-sap-mappings-sdk.py /path/to/hybris The SDK must contain compiled commercewebservices web classes, commerceservices classes and its Spring test/servlet jars. The runner uses the project's cached ASM 9.10.1 and a JDK compatible with the SDK; no new dependency is installed. Synthetic controllers are redefined in a temporary instrumented JVM around the genuine SDK CommerceHandlerMapping . Real Spring request lookup is compared with fresh SDK initialization after mapping removal/move, override addition/removal, lower priority, base fallback and API-version changes, including repeated saves and unrelated routes. It also checks registration-failure rollback, missing-lock/inspection refusal, generated-adapter preservation, sticky added-method refusal across saves, independent context diagnostics, lookup locking during rebuild and ordinary Spring MVC behavior. Add --disable-refresh to compile a temporary copy without the SDK rescan hook; the removed-winner fallback assertion must fail. SDK jars and sources are not copied into the project, and the runner does not start or write a SAP application. The fixture substitutes only configuration-service priority lookup with numeric synthetic keys. It proves priority selection and registry refresh on Spring 5.3.43 and 6.2.12, not property-file reload, live SAP HTTP acceptance, or custom/programmatic mapping discovery.

title: Isolated dynamic-attribute and CronJob reload acceptance
text: Isolated dynamic-attribute and CronJob reload acceptance Run python3 scripts/test_sap_flows_proof.py for the portable acceptance predicate. After ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar , run: bash python3 scripts/test-sap-flows-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar Use the jar version built by your checkout and a JDK compatible with the SDK. The runner reads the SDK Spring version instead of upgrading the project's existing Spring lanes. Genuine SDK dynamic get/set dispatch and job performable results run under the real agent, with v1 → v2 → added-helper v3 → v2 edits. Each step checks fresh HTTP behavior on retained and current instances, exact-byte VERIFY receipts, stable agent session/JVM, and unchanged unrelated behavior. The negative control --withhold-edit must fail; a compiled class never published to the watcher must not be certified as applied. Persistence/type resolution is isolated in memory and jobs are invoked directly. This does not test CronJobService scheduling, stored models, item-type metadata changes, real tenant startup or cluster behavior. Report a live SAP lane separately as unrun unless it was actually executed in an authorized test environment. Cross-check the existing OCC/list-directive/request-mapping runners above, keeping their support boundaries unchanged. No proprietary jars or private source belong in the fixture. See integration acceptance .

title: SAP Solr provider/resolver reload guidance
text: SAP Solr provider/resolver reload guidance A successful code reload for a class implementing SAP Commerce FieldValueProvider , ValueResolver or TypeValueResolver emits a visible INFO advisory: Reclazz did not reindex stored documents. Validate a subsequent indexing operation and explicitly reindex affected documents if needed. The code receipt/VERIFY still describes class bytes only; it is not an indexing receipt. This advice neither requests a JVM restart nor triggers an index operation. Recognition follows implemented interfaces through superclass/interface inheritance. It does not infer index names, document IDs or downstream dependencies of ordinary helper classes. A class name containing Solr or Provider is insufficient. Failure to resolve the loaded hierarchy produces no indexing claim. Absence of a advisory is not evidence that no index can be affected. bash ./gradlew :agent:unitTest --tests '*SapIndexingGuidanceTest' --rerun ./gradlew :agent:e2eTest --tests '*SapIndexingGuidanceTest' --rerun ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar python3 scripts/test-sap-indexing-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar # Negative control: must exit nonzero because edited class bytes are withheld. python3 scripts/test-sap-indexing-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --withhold-edit The portable tests use synthetic interface identities and a snapshot. The optional SDK acceptance instead compiles synthetic application classes against installed SAP interfaces, invokes genuine FieldValue / DefaultSolrInputDocument paths with the real agent, and stores immutable document snapshots locally. It checks method-body edits, a newly added helper method, a revert, same-session exact-byte receipts, changed newly built documents, unchanged older snapshots until explicit reindex, and ordinary-class exclusion. The installed SDK stays outside the repo. This is isolated document-building acceptance, not live Solr or full SAP indexer acceptance. It starts no tenant, indexer CronJob or Solr server, and writes no live index. Schema changes, index configuration, cluster distribution, commit/query visibility and selecting affected documents/indexes remain unverified here.

title: Isolated custom-cache characterization
text: Isolated custom-cache characterization bash ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar python3 scripts/test-sap-caches-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar # Desired-contract probe: currently exits nonzero after proving helper code is live. python3 scripts/test-sap-caches-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --require-fresh-helper # Negative control: unpublished edited bytes must fail the receipt check. python3 scripts/test-sap-caches-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --withhold-edit The optional runner uses installed SDK platform jars and synthetic Spring singleton beans with a genuine Guava cache and an AtomicReference/TTL cache. Observed on Spring 5.3.43 / Guava 33.1.0-jre and Spring 6.2.12 / Guava 33.4.8-jre: Method-body reload Guava owner Custom TTL owner Unrelated caches Registered, autowired bean dependency Fresh result through recreated owner Fresh result through recreated owner Warm entries retained Cache owner itself Fresh result when its owner reloads Fresh result when its owner reloads Warm entries retained Plain static helper, not a Spring bean Old cached result retained Old cached result retained Warm entries retained Subsequent explicit owner edit Fresh result Fresh result Warm entries retained The helper limitation is deliberate characterization, not a freshness pass . Default success means this entire observed matrix was reproduced; the stricter --require-fresh-helper mode exposes the unsupported case as a failure. Each reload requires an applied receipt with the exact edited class hash in the same JVM/session. The helper changes from 1 to 2 and uncached results become 122/222, while warmed cached results remain 121/221. Receipt success alone does not establish cache freshness. Both clocks stay fixed through all reloads, before their 60-second expiry; repeated reads and computation counts establish actual cache hits. An explicit 61-second clock advance finally proves expiry in both target and unrelated caches. Constructor counts, managed consumer references and unrelated singleton identity are checked. No cache hooks or application runtime dependencies were added. Existing Spring bean refresh covers the tested owner/registered-dependency paths; custom caches on plain helper dependencies require separate treatment if immediate freshness is needed. No automatic general invalidation is claimed. This is isolated Spring/Guava acceptance using SDK libraries. It starts no SAP tenant and contacts no external service or cluster. Structural edits, external references to destroyed beans, static/shared caches, FactoryBeans, scoped/prototype owners and concurrent TTL computation are outside this experiment. The simple AtomicReference fixture publishes immutable entries under serial test operations; it is not a concurrency algorithm recommendation.

title: SAP process definition diagnostics
text: SAP process definition diagnostics Changes to local XML referenced by an existing ProcessDefinitionResource singleton in a captured active Spring context produce a WARN : not applied; restart required . This is resource-change guidance, not a successful code reload or a VERIFY receipt. No process definition is refreshed, and no process is started, migrated or replayed. Inspect/validate the changed definition before restarting; restart guidance does not certify that edited XML is valid. Recognition uses the exact registered local path, including arbitrary XML names. The watcher polls registered files outside native roots, subject to existing file and module exclusions. An unregistered *-process.xml is not enough evidence. Closed contexts, remote/packed resources, lazy registrations and FactoryBean products are not claimed. Existing dedicated kinds such as items/backoffice/logging configuration keep their meaning; a registered process with a Spring XML suffix receives process diagnostics instead of being parsed as bean XML. bash ./gradlew :agent:unitTest --tests '*SapProcessResourceRecognitionTest' --rerun ./gradlew :agent:e2eTest --tests '*SapProcessDefinitionDiagnosticTest' --rerun python3 scripts/test-sap-process-sdk.py /path/to/hybris The portable tests use a synthetic API fixture and a real agent/watcher JVM. The SDK runner independently checks genuine resource registrations against the installed Spring/SDK jars after :agent:compileJava . It does not start a tenant, parse a business process or exercise a scheduler. These checks are not live SAP acceptance. Automatic definition refresh requires a separate design: the SDK factory/cache APIs alone do not establish isolation to newly started processes.

title: Isolated SAP event-listener acceptance
text: Isolated SAP event-listener acceptance bash ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar python3 scripts/test-sap-events-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar # Negative control: an unpublished edit must fail the receipt/behavior check. python3 scripts/test-sap-events-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --withhold-edit The runner compiles a synthetic com.example subclass of the genuine SDK AbstractEventListener plus a AbstractEvent and registers it with a real Spring context under the built agent. Events are published through Spring's multicaster, so the SDK's final onApplicationEvent cluster and tenant guard runs before onEvent ; local stub ClusterService / TenantService and a locally scoped event make that guard pass honestly. Editing the listener body and a registered dependency, then reverting, each requires an applied VERIFY receipt with the exact class hash in one JVM/session, and is checked for changed event output, exactly one delivery per publish, preserved listener identity and an unaffected unrelated bean. This confirms the existing hot-swap already covers SAP event-listener reload; no new production hook was needed. It is isolated acceptance, not a live run: it starts no tenant or cluster, sends no external events, and the afterPropertiesSet tenant-scope initialization path is unverified here because it needs live SAP infrastructure.

title: Isolated ConstraintValidator acceptance
text: Isolated ConstraintValidator acceptance bash ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar python3 scripts/test-sap-validators-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar # Negative control: an unpublished edit must fail the receipt/behavior check. python3 scripts/test-sap-validators-sdk.py /path/to/hybris --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --withhold-edit The runner builds a genuine Hibernate Validator (the installed provider, jakarta namespace) with a synthetic constraint, a custom ConstraintValidator and an injected dependency, and validates a bean through the real provider under the built agent. Editing the validator's isValid body and the injected dependency, then reverting, each requires an applied VERIFY receipt with the exact class hash in one JVM/session and is checked for the changed violation message, exactly one validation per request, and an initialize count that stays at one. A stable init count proves the provider keeps a single cached validator instance whose method bodies the agent hot-swaps in place, so the existing SpringValidatorReloader metadata flush is not needed for a body or dependency edit. No new production hook was required. This is isolated acceptance, not a live run. It distinguishes a validator-instance body edit (covered) from constraint-metadata changes (handled separately by the metadata flush) and from structural annotation edits, which stay unverified here along with provider lifecycle beyond instance reuse.

title: Synthetic constructor ownership on installed SDK Spring graphs
text: Synthetic constructor ownership on installed SDK Spring graphs scripts/test-sap-constructor-sdk.py runs agentless fresh startup and cached-constructor controls, then real class-file saves through a held HTTP caller. It uses the installed exact SAP SDK Spring5.3.43/6.2.12 binaries in isolated classpaths and never starts a tenant or writes the SDK tree. The current runner targets local SapMachine17/21 installations on macOS; other JVM/OS layouts need a separately reviewed runner configuration. bash python3 scripts/test-sap-constructor-sdk.py --sdk-search-root /path/to/local/sdks --agent agent/build/libs/agent-1.7.0.jar --output /tmp/reclazz-constructor-results The search root must contain the owner's installed SDK directories. The exact measured spring-beans binary hashes are checked; a missing or different binary is a setup failure, not a behavioral failure. No proprietary JAR is downloaded or bundled. The runner builds only synthetic fixtures in temporary directories, sanitizes SDK paths from logs, closes owned JVMs, and writes per-profile/JDK observations and raw logs to the requested output directory. Use a fresh output directory per run; a lock prevents duplicate drivers writing one result set. Fresh native controls use10/20/30/40. Watcher cases cover direct Owner saves followed by helper-only saves, parent-child helper-only cascade, same-factory recursive destruction, and a withheld-save negative control. Accepted save receipts alone do not pass: exact session/input hashes, current constructor value, current held receiver, native dependency edges and unrelated identity are asserted. The HTTP observer never looks up or recreates a bean to repair the fixture. Exit0 requires all desired/control cases to pass; baseline desired failures remain exit1. The fixture uses @Component to select actual ordinary Spring recreation. A plain programmatic registration without a stereotype can use the agent's helper-body route, so a stale result from that different route is not constructor-transaction causal proof. SDK-derived native graph acceptance must not be labelled live SAP application/tenant acceptance. Ordinary sibling/shadow/refusal/failure/batch controls also live in the inherited ConstructorDependencyContract ; the standard Spring5 and isolated Spring6 test wrappers remain their normal Gradle entry points. SDK execution uses existing test-only JUnit artifacts and keeps them out of runtime distributions.

title: Live SAP runner determinism
text: Live SAP runner determinism ./gradlew :integration-test:harnessContractTest --rerun checks thirteen runner ordering/polling/restoration cases without SAP, using fake socket events, actual runner child JVMs and loopback HTTP. :integration-test:sapProofTest --rerun retains eight model-save acceptance checks. Both are wired into this module's check ; a green portable target is not a live SAP result. Live runs read committed fixture baselines from HEAD, wait for each changed source's own COMPILE then exact-owner RELOAD, poll expected HTTP status and body, and verify final byte-identical restoration. ImpEx must transition from a visible v1 baseline to v2 and back to v1, with terminal import outcomes; stale v2 data cannot establish success. The single nonce-based model-save POST is not retried. Record five identical full runs on one boot plus a fresh-boot run, the exact agent artifact/server identity and the fixture/ImpEx restoration checks. The SAP default suite has 45 scenarios and requires all 45 to PASS; any SKIP is rejected. It contains no Hibernate ORM scenario. The real Hibernate L2 provider regression remains separate in :agent:hibernateTest . See the runner guide for scope and prerequisites. Broader SAP capability coverage remains a separate staged task; these synchronization changes do not certify those capabilities.

title: Product reference
text: Detailed support, compatibility and architecture from the source baseline. Java 17+ is a target requirement, not certification of every JVM, OS or framework. Use the support reference for conditions and the evidence scope for measured environments. For your first reload use the installation guide ; for concise change-specific outcomes use the reload matrix . Why Reclazz? Spring Boot DevTools restarts the application context after a code change. Reclazz is free, open-source , and can redefine classes in the existing JVM. title: Comparison
text: Comparison Feature Reclazz Spring Boot DevTools JRebel Price Free & open source Free Commercial Reload type In-place hot-swap Full context restart In-place hot-swap Application state Retained for in-place body edits; recreated beans lose mutable instance state Lost on restart Preserved Method body changes Yes Yes (restart) Yes Add / remove methods Yes (supported JDK 17+ paths) Yes (restart) Yes Add instance fields Yes , and on a stock JDK an object that already existed reads the initialiser's value on the field's first read: cache = new ArrayList<>() added to a live Spring singleton is a list, not a null. The initialiser is lifted out of the constructor on its own, including isolated conditional expressions in single-constructor classes; one that needs a constructor argument is named instead. Scope . Direct reads/writes from another reloaded watched class use the same store on the measured stock-JDK lanes; see the cross-class scope . On JBR/DCEVM the field is real and objects from before the reload keep the type default Yes (restart) No: "will not be initialized in existing instances" ( FAQ ) Add static fields Yes , constants and isolated initialisers, including ternary and short-circuit expressions. Only the selected branch runs; later saves preserve the field’s current value. Scope Yes (restart) Yes, but the initialiser is not re-run Added static field whose initialiser is entangled with the rest of <clinit> Reads as null/0, and names the field and the reason Yes (restart) Reads as null/0 Add enum values (on the end) Yes on JDK 17-25 : values() , valueOf , switches and the EnumMap/EnumSet built before the reload all see it. What nothing can find: an array your own code sized with values().length before the reload still has the old length, and indexing it by the new constant's ordinal throws. JDK 26 refuses the sun.misc.Unsafe access this needs, so Reclazz falls back to the JDK's own jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe , which JEP 471 does not cover, by opening that package with the agent's own redefineModule ; --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow keeps the first door open and silences the warning Yes (restart) Yes Remove the LAST enum value Yes on JDK 17-25 , the tail moves no ordinal, so values() and valueOf drop it while every survivor keeps its number Yes (restart) Yes Insert or reorder enum values No, that renumbers every ordinal after the change, including @Enumerated columns already in your database. Reclazz refuses and says why Yes (restart) Yes Add / remove an interface Yes on JetBrains Runtime or DCEVM , existing objects included; on a stock JDK it is refused by the JVM and Reclazz names the interface Yes (restart) Yes Change superclass Not applied by Reclazz. Eligible method bodies may reload while the class keeps its old superclass; dependent methods stay pinned, and unsafe signatures/constructors refuse the whole save. Restart for the hierarchy change. Versioned evidence and limits Yes (restart) Not verified by this research Spring bean refresh Yes (singleton destroy + recreate) Yes (restart) Yes @Bean method added after startup Yes on a stock JDK , for direct instance or static @Bean factories on @Configuration(proxyBeanMethods=false) : object return and one unproxied configuration singleton. Parameters support reference beans, typed collections/maps, reference arrays, Optional , Spring providers and direct @Value , including primitives. Scalar @Value inputs can also refresh an existing unproxied singleton on a checked property save ( scope ). Multiple names register one singleton with aliases. Direct @Primary / @Qualifier participates in Spring argument selection. Direct @Lazy creates the bean on first access, @Scope("prototype") gives every lookup a new instance, and @Profile registers the bean only when the environment accepts it, re-evaluated on a later save. Default @Configuration also supports overridable instance factories with these parameters: inter-bean calls resolve the container singleton and preserve supported explicit-argument/prototype semantics. Static factories retain plain Java call semantics. Later saves replace the product and update its metadata; removal deletes only Reclazz-owned registrations. Existing names are refused. Direct method-level @Conditional evaluates saved metadata against the live context before registration and re-evaluates on later configuration saves. Direct Boot @ConditionalOnProperty , @ConditionalOnBean and @ConditionalOnMissingBean also use native conditions, verified with Boot 2.7.18 / Spring 5.3.39. Other composed condition annotations, web/custom scopes and scoped proxies stay on restart.
